extraction.body: International governments and agencies have urged websites to address two critical cyber-security flaws in a programming language which powers much of the internet. The vulnerabilities were found within the PHP programming language, with a fix issued on Wednesday afternoon. Multiple cyber-security agencies have urged organisations unable to apply fixes in time to consider taking their sites down, leaving bodies such as the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC to take pages offline. The flaws were discovered by AI, with cyber-security firm Wiz saying they were the "most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered" by the tech, which is reshaping the cyber landscape. Finland has temporarily shut down the government's public web services, while the Netherlands' cyber-security agency said it was taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities. The US National Security Agency issued similar advice on X , external for organisations to take their systems offline if they were unable to update with the fix. "These vulnerabilities often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database," it wrote. The Wikimedia Foundation, which runs the online encyclopedia Wikipedia, said it was addressing the security vulnerabilities. "We have taken down a number of other systems as a precautionary measure until they can be safely patched," it said. That led some people to be unable to access parts of Wikipedia on Wednesday. They have not confirmed a link to PHP - BBC News has approached them for comment. Other websites, including the art platform DeviantArt, have said they are " temporarily down for maintenance , external " without specifying the reason. The vulnerabilities were discovered by cyber-security researchers at the firms Calif and Wiz. Through that program, they were given access to the AI company's advanced AI tools in order to find and fix flaws in web development language. OpenAI said in a blog post , external that the discovery was "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory". It added an internal researcher at the company had also discovered the issue around the same time as the other firms. The flaws had gone undetected for more than a decade. By August, after a few weeks of using advanced AI tools, they were discovered. "Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours," Wiz said in a blog post. It has estimated "roughly 70%" of the internet is affected, though the BBC is unable to verify that figure. It forced PHP Foundation to rush out its announcement of the vulnerability and its huge scale. The Netherlands' National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, an agency of the Dutch government, has taken down its website. Similarly the website of the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of the nation's parliament, has become inaccessible. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia have urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes. "Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated," the NCSC said in a note , external . Japan's national cyber-security office and EU cyber-security officials have issued a similar warning , external . "PHP is everywhere. It ​quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful ⁠lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," cyber-security company Huntress said. Cyber-security expert Don Smith, from the Sophos Counter Threat Unit, told the BBC this would "likely be a priority target" for hackers. The immediate challenge was not simply installing a patch to fix the issue, but finding and managing every instance where PHP was running, he said. "The use of PHP is pervasive, it can sit beneath public websites, content management systems, hosting platforms and third-party products, sometimes without even being obvious to the organisation using it," he said. He said it was crucial that organisations looked out for signs that an attacker "might have already have gained a foothold". Dane Knecht, chief technology officer at internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, said he was , external "seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up". The NCSC said once organisations have installed the update, they should "continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP". It is not yet clear which versions of the programming language are affected, but CERT-EU said it could affect all versions of it dating back to PHP 5 onwards - which launched in 2004. extraction.body: Cyber security chiefs have warned UK organisations their websites may have to be taken offline, after a researcher using AI discovered a "critical security issue" in a programming language. The Finnish government's website was one of several to be partly disabled because of the incident on Wednesday, along with the websites of several local authorities in the UK. Oxford City Council and the City of Edinburgh Council were among the organisations to take their websites offline, while pages for some BBC programmes were unavailable. The Office for Budget Responsibility said it had followed guidance to take its website offline, "in view of the critical security issues affecting PHP". It is understood some of the government's online services may be temporarily unavailable while steps are taken to maintain security, but any impact is expected to be minimal. PHP is a language used by the majority of websites. Credit: iStock No large public-facing critical services are thought to have been affected. The security issue identified by the researcher could allow attackers to remotely control any web servers running the widely used programming language, PHP. PHP is used by almost 70% of websites, according cybersecurity firm Cloudflare, and underpins popular platforms such as WordPress and Magento. Organisations have been urged by the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) to update to a new, fixed version of the software. If software cannot be immediately upgraded, organisations should consider taking their websites offline, the NCSC said. A government spokesperson said: "Work is already under way across government to actively identify and patch any potential exposure. "We encourage all organisations, private and public, large and small, to follow guidance issued by the NCSC to understand their exposure and take the necessary actions to safeguard their systems." The cyber division of the National Security Agency in the US warned weaknesses in the software could provide "a direct path to the server's file system or database". The Wall Street Journal reported that the flaw was discovered in August by Ryan Austin, a researcher at the cybersecurity company Calif, using an advanced AI model developed by OpenAI. PHP developers had reportedly planned a security update on Thursday, but the release was brought forward after details of its work to address the vulnerabilities leaked online. OpenAI, which runs ChatGPT, said in the past two months it has been leading a team of researchers working to address the critical flaw in PHP, and supported its developers as it led the fixes. The company described the incident as "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory", adding that while AI can help to uncover issues, it can also aid attackers. "To our knowledge, frontier AI found these vulnerabilities before attackers did, opening a defender's window for maintainers and security providers to prepare fixes and protections ahead of disclosure," it said. Former head of the NCSC, Ciaran Martin, told Times Radio the vulnerabilities in PHP had the potential to create a significant loss of personal data. He said: "You're talking about the potential to take the personal details of cards, including those crucial three digits on the back and so forth, so people will want to be on the alert for scams in future. "There's more scope for that. You're talking potentially for ransomware attackers, not to be able to do ransomware directly as a result of this, but to get a foothold into the organisation. extraction.body: International governments and agencies have urged websites to address two critical cyber-security flaws in a programming language which powers much of the internet. The vulnerabilities were found within the PHP programming language, with a fix issued on Wednesday afternoon. Multiple cyber-security agencies have urged organisations unable to apply fixes in time to consider taking their sites down, leaving bodies such as the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC to take pages offline. The flaws were discovered by AI, with cyber-security firm Wiz saying they were the "most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered" by the tech, which is reshaping the cyber landscape. Finland has temporarily shut down the government's public web services, while the Netherlands' cyber-security agency said it was taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities. The US National Security Agency issued similar advice on X , external for organisations to take their systems offline if they were unable to update with the fix. "These vulnerabilities often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database," it wrote. The Wikimedia Foundation, which runs the online encyclopedia Wikipedia, said it was addressing the security vulnerabilities. "We have taken down a number of other systems as a precautionary measure until they can be safely patched," it said. That led some people to be unable to access parts of Wikipedia on Wednesday. They have not confirmed a link to PHP - BBC News has approached them for comment. Other websites, including the art platform DeviantArt, have said they are " temporarily down for maintenance , external " without specifying the reason. The vulnerabilities were discovered by cyber-security researchers at the firms Calif and Wiz. Through that program, they were given access to the AI company's advanced AI tools in order to find and fix flaws in web development language. OpenAI said in a blog post , external that the discovery was "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory". It added an internal researcher at the company had also discovered the issue around the same time as the other firms. The flaws had gone undetected for more than a decade. By August, after a few weeks of using advanced AI tools, they were discovered. "Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours," Wiz said in a blog post. It has estimated "roughly 70%" of the internet is affected, though the BBC is unable to verify that figure. It forced PHP Foundation to rush out its announcement of the vulnerability and its huge scale. The Netherlands' National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, an agency of the Dutch government, has taken down its website. Similarly the website of the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of the nation's parliament, has become inaccessible. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia have urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes. "Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated," the NCSC said in a note , external . Japan's national cyber-security office and EU cyber-security officials have issued a similar warning , external . "PHP is everywhere. It ​quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful ⁠lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," cyber-security company Huntress said. Cyber-security expert Don Smith, from the Sophos Counter Threat Unit, told the BBC this would "likely be a priority target" for hackers. The immediate challenge was not simply installing a patch to fix the issue, but finding and managing every instance where PHP was running, he said. "The use of PHP is pervasive, it can sit beneath public websites, content management systems, hosting platforms and third-party products, sometimes without even being obvious to the organisation using it," he said. He said it was crucial that organisations looked out for signs that an attacker "might have already have gained a foothold". Dane Knecht, chief technology officer at internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, said he was , external "seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up". The NCSC said once organisations have installed the update, they should "continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP". It is not yet clear which versions of the programming language are affected, but CERT-EU said it could affect all versions of it dating back to PHP 5 onwards - which launched in 2004. extraction.body: Cyber security chiefs have warned UK organisations their websites may have to be taken offline, after a researcher using AI discovered a "critical security issue" in a programming language. The Finnish government's website was one of several to be partly disabled because of the incident on Wednesday, along with the websites of several local authorities in the UK. Oxford City Council and the City of Edinburgh Council were among the organisations to take their websites offline, while pages for some BBC programmes were unavailable. The Office for Budget Responsibility said it had followed guidance to take its website offline, "in view of the critical security issues affecting PHP". It is understood some of the government's online services may be temporarily unavailable while steps are taken to maintain security, but any impact is expected to be minimal. PHP is a language used by the majority of websites. Credit: iStock No large public-facing critical services are thought to have been affected. The security issue identified by the researcher could allow attackers to remotely control any web servers running the widely used programming language, PHP. PHP is used by almost 70% of websites, according cybersecurity firm Cloudflare, and underpins popular platforms such as WordPress and Magento. Organisations have been urged by the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) to update to a new, fixed version of the software. If software cannot be immediately upgraded, organisations should consider taking their websites offline, the NCSC said. A government spokesperson said: "Work is already under way across government to actively identify and patch any potential exposure. "We encourage all organisations, private and public, large and small, to follow guidance issued by the NCSC to understand their exposure and take the necessary actions to safeguard their systems." The cyber division of the National Security Agency in the US warned weaknesses in the software could provide "a direct path to the server's file system or database". The Wall Street Journal reported that the flaw was discovered in August by Ryan Austin, a researcher at the cybersecurity company Calif, using an advanced AI model developed by OpenAI. PHP developers had reportedly planned a security update on Thursday, but the release was brought forward after details of its work to address the vulnerabilities leaked online. OpenAI, which runs ChatGPT, said in the past two months it has been leading a team of researchers working to address the critical flaw in PHP, and supported its developers as it led the fixes. The company described the incident as "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory", adding that while AI can help to uncover issues, it can also aid attackers. "To our knowledge, frontier AI found these vulnerabilities before attackers did, opening a defender's window for maintainers and security providers to prepare fixes and protections ahead of disclosure," it said. Former head of the NCSC, Ciaran Martin, told Times Radio the vulnerabilities in PHP had the potential to create a significant loss of personal data. He said: "You're talking about the potential to take the personal details of cards, including those crucial three digits on the back and so forth, so people will want to be on the alert for scams in future. "There's more scope for that. You're talking potentially for ransomware attackers, not to be able to do ransomware directly as a result of this, but to get a foothold into the organisation. extraction.body: The PHP development team has released emergency security updates to fix PHP2Shell, two critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) that could let attackers execute code remotely on web servers without logging in. The fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, and the team is strongly urging all PHP users to update immediately. “These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit,” Wiz researchers explained . Every PHP installation that serves web requests is affected, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. Setups using mod_php face the greatest danger. A working exploit has already shown that a single unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs. “The PHP situation will lead to a mass of incidents – it’s one of the biggest vulns in years,” noted security researcher Kevin Beaumont. CVE-2026-109618 – RCE via OOM corruption : out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid. CVE-2026-109619 – RCE via stale global state : request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it. The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) is urging organizations to consider taking offline any system that can’t be fixed right away. “So many embedded installations out there that will never be patched. Too many forgotten, unmaintained apps. There will be a long tail for this one,” commented computer forensics expert Hal Pomeranz. Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. Downloads are available here . Linux distributions and long-term support (LTS) vendors got the patches ahead of the public release, so admins should check with their vendor for updated packages. Anyone who relies on rpms.remirepo.net , a volunteer-maintained repository, is advised to switch to distribution packages or build PHP from source so they can patch immediately. The repository will not have updates available today. Because the vulnerabilities are so severe, the PHP security team has also released minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1. These are meant for people who build from source or who don’t have an LTS vendor. “PHP sites behind Cloudflare already have an initial set of WAF rules deployed for the known exploit vectors in these vulnerabilities. The rules are available to all customers, including free,” said Dane Knecht, CTO at Cloudflare.

sources.title: PHP2Shell: AI uncovers critical RCE vulnerabilities affecting 70% of the Internet - wiz.io
passages: With 70% of the Internet affected, the impact of PHP2Shell cannot be overstated.
The vulnerable code had been there for more than a decade – what AI changed was the ability to understand the weaknesses and turn them into a working exploit.
With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work.
Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security.
In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet.
In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify.
We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities.
Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging.
Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours.
As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice.
Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world.
Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them.
Sensor customers using the newest version (1.0.12768) can also enable a built-in response policy to automatically terminate processes exhibiting behaviors typical of PHP2Shell exploitation:
Notably, Gemini 4 Argon made an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch.

Wiz customers should refer to the Wiz Threat Intel Center advisory for PHP2Shell , which includes built-in coverage for agentless and runtime vulnerability detection, exploitation detection via Wiz Defend and Sensor, and automatic response policies, alongside remediation and threat hunting guidance.

These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it , putting every affected website in immediate risk.
Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4.
Below you can find a table that demonstrates what type of impact was demonstrated by each of the bugs we reported to PHP.
The applications listed below are targets we chose for the RCE demonstrations.
Demonstrations of PHP2Shell with Wordpress, Joomla, and Drupal:
For over a decade, these critical vulnerabilities remained unaddressed because vulnerability discovery and exploitation were incredibly complex.
August 24, 2026: Wiz Research reports the vulnerabilities to the PHP security team.

We combined these vulnerabilities into a single exploit script, php2shell, and demonstrated that it could execute code remotely without authentication on deployments of WordPress ( wordpress:latest ), Drupal ( drupal:latest ), and Joomla ( joomla:latest ), using their latest container images at the time of testing.
Wiz researchers will walk through what we've discovered, how we found these vulnerabilities, and what security teams need to know to assess their exposure and respond.

extraction.body: FORT MEADE, Md. — PHP — short for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor — works on most major operating systems. It runs directly on web servers and can be added into HTML to create dynamic web pages. Because PHP is so widely used, these security flaws can create an environment ripe for exploitation. We are prioritizing identification of malicious cyber actors that may seek to exploit these vulnerabilities, collectively nicknamed “PHP2Shell,” and recommend organizations take the following precautions. What Should be Done? It will be critical in the coming weeks to maintain heightened awareness of your internet-facing devices and services that are reliant on PHP. It is essential for all to prioritize incorporating vendor patches that may be explicitly tied to the PHP2Shell issues. All users should immediately conduct an inventory, where feasible, of hardware/software services reliant on now-vulnerable PHP versions. Vigilance in applying patches related to those systems is paramount. PHP released their open-source software patch Wednesday, October 21, 2026. Additional software vendors may also publish patches once they are available. It’s imperative to closely monitor these updates. Information on the latest mitigations and patching guidance is available on the PHP.net Security Advisory page . While vendors work to patch their individual software packages, it is important for organizations to assess whether additional mitigation steps should be taken such as: Adding enhanced logging within network/operational environments Replacing end-of-life PHP services which will not be compatible with patching If an immediate update is not feasible, it is recommended that organizations take the system offline until it can be fully mitigated. Why is this an Issue? “PHP2Shell” could allow attackers to take control of affected web servers without prior access or authentication. Such an access vector could help attackers steal sensitive data, disrupt services, or move deeper into a network. These vulnerabilities are flaws in PHP itself, not in the hosted application or its configuration. Servers running affected PHP versions are exploitable. Cyber actors are likely to weaponize PHP2Shell vulnerabilities. These risks are serious enough to require immediate patching across United States Government departments and agencies. The Way Forward NSA will continue to work with experts across the intelligence community (IC), including CISA, to identify and address potential U.S. Government and National Security Service vulnerabilities. We stand with our warfighters and our domestic and foreign partners to improve our collective cyber defenses and threat detection. extraction.body: PHP has released security updates for two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Apache mod_php deployments warrant immediate attention: PHP reports a demonstrated exploit that can trigger before application code runs. The vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each carry a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2. Cloudflare has reported attack traffic targeting these vulnerabilities, including attempts to evade its protections. Organizations should prioritize updates for internet-facing PHP deployments, starting with Apache mod_php. PHP identifies installations serving web requests as at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed. Exploitability varies by configuration and application behavior. Both flaws involve PHP’s handling of memory and internal request state. Researchers have also demonstrated unauthenticated disclosure of PHP worker memory. Exposed memory can contain passwords, authentication tokens, and API keys. The following upstream releases address both vulnerabilities: For distribution-managed installations, use your vendor’s advisory to identify the fixed package. Backported fixes may retain an older upstream version number. PHP 8.1 and earlier remain outside regular upstream support. PHP has provided limited source backports for 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1 . Organizations running those branches should obtain a fixed build from their distribution or support vendor, apply the appropriate source backport, or upgrade to a supported release. Qualys customers can begin discovery with QID 45110 — PHP Server Detected , an Information Gathered (IG) check. QID 45110 identifies PHP installations; it does not confirm vulnerability to either CVE. Use its results to identify systems for review, then validate each installation against the applicable PHP or vendor advisory. Qualys CyberSecurity Asset Management (CSAM) can help teams inventory PHP installations, identify end-of-life software, and prioritize internet-facing assets for remediation. Qualys released the following detection QIDs: The QIDs listed above are now available. We will add distribution-specific detection QIDs to this blog as they are released. After remediation, rerun the applicable checks and verify that both the installed packages and running PHP instances include the fixes. This mitigation follows PHP’s mitigation guidance, with additional insights from the Qualys Threat Research Unit (TRU). This mitigation disables the PHP session upload-progress feature across every web-facing PHP runtime on the host, and hardens the related session-handling configuration. This removes the vulnerable code path from execution without changing the application itself. This is an interim risk-reduction measure that eliminates reachability of the flaw. Customers can use QID 389102 to assess PHP2Shell exposure. To broaden visibility into PHP installations outside standard locations, customers can also enable Qualys Deep Scan. Deep Scan identifies vulnerable PHP binaries in custom application folders, secondary drives, and other configured directories. Findings appear in VMDR with the full binary path, installed version, and recommended fixed version , giving security and IT teams the details needed to locate and remediate overlooked installations. With Qualys InstaScan, powered by Agent Insta, new vendor advisories become actionable exposure findings using the software inventory your environment already reports. InstaScan continuously matches advisory intelligence against that inventory, surfacing findings for assets in scope—typically within minutes of advisory processing, without requiring a new scan. Your team can begin investigating and prioritizing remediation while the next scheduled scan is still hours away. For PHP2Shell, this brings faster visibility as distribution-specific advisories become available. coreStoryFacts.text: The PHP development team has released emergency security updates to fix PHP2Shell, two critical vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619) that could let attackers execute code remotely on web servers without logging in.
The fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, and the team is strongly urging all PHP users to update immediately.
With 70% of the Internet affected, the impact of PHP2Shell cannot be overstated.
The vulnerable code had been there for more than a decade – what AI changed was the ability to understand the weaknesses and turn them into a working exploit.
With frontier AI models and the right tools, a single researcher completed in a week what previously would have taken a world-class team months of work.
Some vulnerabilities become turning points because they challenge fundamental assumptions about security.
In 2014, Heartbleed exposed the fragility of shared infrastructure securing the internet.
In 2021, Log4Shell revealed how deeply embedded software dependencies could create widespread exposure that organizations struggled to identify.
We believe PHP2Shell could mark a similar turning point for the AI era, illustrating how AI can change the practical exploitability of longstanding vulnerabilities.
Building the exploit required chaining multiple flaws and adapting to each target’s memory layout through repeated testing and debugging.
Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours.
As the time and expertise required for this work decrease, complexity may no longer provide a meaningful barrier, changing how we define what is vulnerable in practice.
Wiz Research uncovered multiple critical vulnerabilities in core PHP, a popular general-purpose scripting language that powers 70% of all websites in the world.
Successful exploitation could allow attackers to take control of affected servers, steal sensitive data, and deface the websites running on them.
Sensor customers using the newest version (1.0.12768) can also enable a built-in response policy to automatically terminate processes exhibiting behaviors typical of PHP2Shell exploitation:
Notably, Gemini 4 Argon made an invaluable contribution to finding the vulnerability, exploit development, attack detection, and validation of the patch.

Wiz customers should refer to the Wiz Threat Intel Center advisory for PHP2Shell , which includes built-in coverage for agentless and runtime vulnerability detection, exploitation detection via Wiz Defend and Sensor, and automatic response policies, alongside remediation and threat hunting guidance.

These vulnerabilities include memory disclosure and unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP itself, independent of the application running on top of it , putting every affected website in immediate risk.
Every PHP version released in the last decade is affected by at least one of these vulnerabilities, going back to version 5.4.
Below you can find a table that demonstrates what type of impact was demonstrated by each of the bugs we reported to PHP.
The applications listed below are targets we chose for the RCE demonstrations.

For over a decade, these critical vulnerabilities remained unaddressed because vulnerability discovery and exploitation were incredibly complex.
August 24, 2026: Wiz Research reports the vulnerabilities to the PHP security team.

The fixes are in PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, and the team is strongly urging all PHP users to update immediately. “These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. Frontier AI models substantially reduced that barrier, turning a longstanding flaw into an exploit,” Wiz researchers explained . Every PHP installation that serves web requests is affected, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. Setups using mod_php face the greatest danger. A working exploit has already shown that a single unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs. “The PHP situation will lead to a mass of incidents – it’s one of the biggest vulns in years,” noted security researcher Kevin Beaumont. CVE-2026-109618 – RCE via OOM corruption : out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid. CVE-2026-109619 – RCE via stale global state : request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it. The UK’s National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) is urging organizations to consider taking offline any system that can’t be fixed right away. “So many embedded installations out there that will never be patched. Too many forgotten, unmaintained apps. There will be a long tail for this one,” commented computer forensics expert Hal Pomeranz. Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. Downloads are available here . Linux distributions and long-term support (LTS) vendors got the patches ahead of the public release, so admins should check with their vendor for updated packages. Anyone who relies on rpms.remirepo.net , a volunteer-maintained repository, is advised to switch to distribution packages or build PHP from source so they can patch immediately. The repository will not have updates available today. Because the vulnerabilities are so severe, the PHP security team has also released minimal source backports for PHP 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1. These are meant for people who build from source or who don’t have an LTS vendor. “PHP sites behind Cloudflare already have an initial set of WAF rules deployed for the known exploit vectors in these vulnerabilities. The rules are available to all customers, including free,” said Dane Knecht, CTO at Cloudflare.

Immediate patching is strongly advised. On October 21, 2026, PHP released the patch fixing multiple memory-safety vulnerabilities in the core engine. These findings rank among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered in PHP, and arguably in software history. The underlying flaws had been present for decades, but demonstrating their exploitability required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve. extraction.body: FORT MEADE, Md. — PHP — short for PHP: Hypertext Preprocessor — works on most major operating systems. It runs directly on web servers and can be added into HTML to create dynamic web pages. Because PHP is so widely used, these security flaws can create an environment ripe for exploitation. We are prioritizing identification of malicious cyber actors that may seek to exploit these vulnerabilities, collectively nicknamed “PHP2Shell,” and recommend organizations take the following precautions. What Should be Done? It will be critical in the coming weeks to maintain heightened awareness of your internet-facing devices and services that are reliant on PHP. It is essential for all to prioritize incorporating vendor patches that may be explicitly tied to the PHP2Shell issues. All users should immediately conduct an inventory, where feasible, of hardware/software services reliant on now-vulnerable PHP versions. Vigilance in applying patches related to those systems is paramount. PHP released their open-source software patch Wednesday, October 21, 2026. Additional software vendors may also publish patches once they are available. It’s imperative to closely monitor these updates. Information on the latest mitigations and patching guidance is available on the PHP.net Security Advisory page . While vendors work to patch their individual software packages, it is important for organizations to assess whether additional mitigation steps should be taken such as: Adding enhanced logging within network/operational environments Replacing end-of-life PHP services which will not be compatible with patching If an immediate update is not feasible, it is recommended that organizations take the system offline until it can be fully mitigated. Why is this an Issue? “PHP2Shell” could allow attackers to take control of affected web servers without prior access or authentication. Such an access vector could help attackers steal sensitive data, disrupt services, or move deeper into a network. These vulnerabilities are flaws in PHP itself, not in the hosted application or its configuration. Servers running affected PHP versions are exploitable. Cyber actors are likely to weaponize PHP2Shell vulnerabilities. These risks are serious enough to require immediate patching across United States Government departments and agencies. The Way Forward NSA will continue to work with experts across the intelligence community (IC), including CISA, to identify and address potential U.S. Government and National Security Service vulnerabilities. We stand with our warfighters and our domestic and foreign partners to improve our collective cyber defenses and threat detection. extraction.body: PHP has released security updates for two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. Apache mod_php deployments warrant immediate attention: PHP reports a demonstrated exploit that can trigger before application code runs. The vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each carry a CVSS v4.0 score of 9.2. Cloudflare has reported attack traffic targeting these vulnerabilities, including attempts to evade its protections. Organizations should prioritize updates for internet-facing PHP deployments, starting with Apache mod_php. PHP identifies installations serving web requests as at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP, and LiteSpeed. Exploitability varies by configuration and application behavior. Both flaws involve PHP’s handling of memory and internal request state. Researchers have also demonstrated unauthenticated disclosure of PHP worker memory. Exposed memory can contain passwords, authentication tokens, and API keys. The following upstream releases address both vulnerabilities: For distribution-managed installations, use your vendor’s advisory to identify the fixed package. Backported fixes may retain an older upstream version number. PHP 8.1 and earlier remain outside regular upstream support. PHP has provided limited source backports for 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1 . Organizations running those branches should obtain a fixed build from their distribution or support vendor, apply the appropriate source backport, or upgrade to a supported release. Qualys customers can begin discovery with QID 45110 — PHP Server Detected , an Information Gathered (IG) check. QID 45110 identifies PHP installations; it does not confirm vulnerability to either CVE. Use its results to identify systems for review, then validate each installation against the applicable PHP or vendor advisory. Qualys CyberSecurity Asset Management (CSAM) can help teams inventory PHP installations, identify end-of-life software, and prioritize internet-facing assets for remediation. Qualys released the following detection QIDs: The QIDs listed above are now available. We will add distribution-specific detection QIDs to this blog as they are released. After remediation, rerun the applicable checks and verify that both the installed packages and running PHP instances include the fixes. This mitigation follows PHP’s mitigation guidance, with additional insights from the Qualys Threat Research Unit (TRU). This mitigation disables the PHP session upload-progress feature across every web-facing PHP runtime on the host, and hardens the related session-handling configuration. This removes the vulnerable code path from execution without changing the application itself. This is an interim risk-reduction measure that eliminates reachability of the flaw. Customers can use QID 389102 to assess PHP2Shell exposure. To broaden visibility into PHP installations outside standard locations, customers can also enable Qualys Deep Scan. Deep Scan identifies vulnerable PHP binaries in custom application folders, secondary drives, and other configured directories. Findings appear in VMDR with the full binary path, installed version, and recommended fixed version , giving security and IT teams the details needed to locate and remediate overlooked installations. With Qualys InstaScan, powered by Agent Insta, new vendor advisories become actionable exposure findings using the software inventory your environment already reports. InstaScan continuously matches advisory intelligence against that inventory, surfacing findings for assets in scope—typically within minutes of advisory processing, without requiring a new scan. Your team can begin investigating and prioritizing remediation while the next scheduled scan is still hours away. For PHP2Shell, this brings faster visibility as distribution-specific advisories become available. Supported advisory sources include Red Hat, Ubuntu, Debian, and Oracle Linux, helping teams respond across mixed Linux environments. Use QID 45110 — PHP Server Detected to establish your PHP discovery baseline, keep software inventory current, and configure InstaScan to cover the relevant assets. Use the applicable vulnerability detection QIDs to assess PHP2Shell exposure and verify remediation. Updating is the only complete fix. The following measures, drawn from PHP’s release announcement and detailed security advisories, reduce exposure to specific attack paths. They do not make an unpatched installation safe. CVE-2026-109618: Out-of-Memory Corruption Setting memory_limit=-1 removes PHP’s per-request memory cap and increases the risk of resource exhaustion. Treat it as a temporary measure and account for available resources and worker-level limits. If a patched build cannot be deployed promptly, consider restricting public access or temporarily isolating the affected service while remediation is arranged. Assign an owner and a remediation deadline to each system awaiting an update. Installing a package is one step. Verify that each application is actually using the patched runtime. extraction.body: International governments and agencies have urged websites to address two critical cyber-security flaws in a programming language which powers much of the internet. The vulnerabilities were found within the PHP programming language, with a fix issued on Wednesday afternoon. Multiple cyber-security agencies have urged organisations unable to apply fixes in time to consider taking their sites down, leaving bodies such as the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC to take pages offline. The flaws were discovered by AI, with cyber-security firm Wiz saying they were the "most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered" by the tech, which is reshaping the cyber landscape. Finland has temporarily shut down the government's public web services, while the Netherlands' cyber-security agency said it was taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities. The US National Security Agency issued similar advice on X for organisations to take their systems offline if they were unable to update with the fix. "These vulnerabilities often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database," it wrote. Meanwhile, the White House said federal agencies were working with leading AI labs to speed up a fix to the issue. And in a post on X , Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged people to check if their publicly available websites ran on PHP. The Wikimedia Foundation, which runs the online encyclopedia Wikipedia, said it was addressing the security vulnerabilities. "We have taken down a number of other systems as a precautionary measure until they can be safely patched," it said. That led some people to be unable to access parts of Wikipedia on Wednesday. They have not confirmed a link to PHP - BBC News has approached them for comment. Other websites, including the art platform DeviantArt, have said they are " temporarily down for maintenance " without specifying the reason. The vulnerabilities were discovered by cyber-security researchers at the firms Calif and Wiz. Calif, along with PHP Foundation, were part of a program started by OpenAI called Patch the Planet. Through that program, they were given access to the AI company's advanced AI tools in order to find and fix flaws in web development language. OpenAI said in a blog post that the discovery was "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory". It added an internal researcher at the company had also discovered the issue around the same time as the other firms. The flaws had gone undetected for more than a decade. By August, after a few weeks of using advanced AI tools, they were discovered. "Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours," Wiz said in a blog post. It has estimated "roughly 70%" of the internet is affected, though the BBC is unable to verify that figure. It forced PHP Foundation to rush out its announcement of the vulnerability and its huge scale. The Netherlands' National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, an agency of the Dutch government, has taken down its website. Similarly the website of the Tweede Kamer, the lower house of the nation's parliament, has become inaccessible. The UK's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), as well as its counterparts in the EU and Australia have urged those who use PHP to apply the fixes. "Where immediate remediation is not feasible, organisations should consider taking the system offline until it can be fully mitigated," the NCSC said in a note . Japan's national cyber-security office and EU cyber-security officials have issued a similar warning . "PHP is everywhere. It ​quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful ⁠lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood," cyber-security company Huntress said. Cyber-security expert Don Smith, from the Sophos Counter Threat Unit, told the BBC this would "likely be a priority target" for hackers. The immediate challenge was not simply installing a patch to fix the issue, but finding and managing every instance where PHP was running, he said. "The use of PHP is pervasive, it can sit beneath public websites, content management systems, hosting platforms and third-party products, sometimes without even being obvious to the organisation using it," he said. He said it was crucial that organisations looked out for signs that an attacker "might have already have gained a foothold". The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said the risk scores given to the vulnerabilities "indicate the potential for unauthenticated remote code execution". Such a cyber-attack could potentially allow hackers to install malware and take down websites. Dane Knecht, chief technology officer at internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, said he was "seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up". The NCSC said once organisations have installed the update, they should "continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP".

extraction.body: Cyber security chiefs have warned UK organisations their websites may have to be taken offline, after a researcher using AI discovered a "critical security issue" in a programming language. The Finnish government's website was one of several to be partly disabled because of the incident on Wednesday, along with the websites of several local authorities in the UK. Oxford City Council and the City of Edinburgh Council were among the organisations to take their websites offline, while pages for some BBC programmes were unavailable. The Office for Budget Responsibility said it had followed guidance to take its website offline, "in view of the critical security issues affecting PHP". The security issue identified by the researcher could allow attackers to remotely control any web servers running the widely used programming language, PHP. PHP is used by almost 70% of websites, according cybersecurity firm Cloudflare, and underpins popular platforms such as WordPress and Magento. Organisations have been urged by the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) to update to a new, fixed version of the software. If software cannot be immediately upgraded, organisations should consider taking their websites offline, the NCSC said. The cyber division of the National Security Agency in the US warned weaknesses in the software could provide "a direct path to the server's file system or database". The Wall Street Journal reported that the flaw was discovered in August by Ryan Austin, a researcher at the cybersecurity company Calif, using an advanced AI model developed by OpenAI. PHP developers had reportedly planned a security update on Thursday, but the release was brought forward after details of its work to address the vulnerabilities leaked online. OpenAI, which runs ChatGPT, said in the past two months it has been leading a team of researchers working to address the critical flaw in PHP, and supported its developers as it led the fixes. The company described the incident as "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory", adding that while AI can help to uncover issues, it can also aid attackers. "To our knowledge, frontier AI found these vulnerabilities before attackers did, opening a defender's window for maintainers and security providers to prepare fixes and protections ahead of disclosure," it said. Former head of the NCSC, Ciaran Martin, told Times Radio the vulnerabilities in PHP had the potential to create a significant loss of personal data. He said: "You're talking about the potential to take the personal details of cards, including those crucial three digits on the back and so forth, so people will want to be on the alert for scams in future. "There's more scope for that. You're talking potentially for ransomware attackers, not to be able to do ransomware directly as a result of this, but to get a foothold into the organisation. "You're talking about easier to impersonate CEOs because you get to know them better. All that sort of scamming and fraud and so forth gets turbocharged."

Multiple cyber-security agencies have urged organisations unable to apply fixes in time to consider taking their sites down, leaving bodies such as the Finnish government, Edinburgh council and the BBC to take pages offline. The flaws were discovered by AI, with cyber-security firm Wiz saying they were the "most severe vulnerabilities ever discovered" by the tech, which is reshaping the cyber landscape. Finland has temporarily shut down the government's public web services, while the Netherlands' cyber-security agency said it was taking its own website offline due to the vulnerabilities. The US National Security Agency issued similar advice on X for organisations to take their systems offline if they were unable to update with the fix. "These vulnerabilities often provide a direct path to the server's file system or database," it wrote. Meanwhile, the White House said federal agencies were working with leading AI labs to speed up a fix to the issue. And in a post on X , Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi urged people to check if their publicly available websites ran on PHP. The Wikimedia Foundation, which runs the online encyclopedia Wikipedia, said it was addressing the security vulnerabilities. "We have taken down a number of other systems as a precautionary measure until they can be safely patched," it said. That led some people to be unable to access parts of Wikipedia on Wednesday. They have not confirmed a link to PHP - BBC News has approached them for comment. Other websites, including the art platform DeviantArt, have said they are " temporarily down for maintenance " without specifying the reason. The vulnerabilities were discovered by cyber-security researchers at the firms Calif and Wiz. Calif, along with PHP Foundation, were part of a program started by OpenAI called Patch the Planet. Through that program, they were given access to the AI company's advanced AI tools in order to find and fix flaws in web development language. OpenAI said in a blog post that the discovery was "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory". It added an internal researcher at the company had also discovered the issue around the same time as the other firms. The flaws had gone undetected for more than a decade. By August, after a few weeks of using advanced AI tools, they were discovered. "Frontier models were critical to making this process practical, enabling us to develop and adapt working exploits across multiple applications in hours," Wiz said in a blog post. It has estimated "roughly 70%" of the internet is affected, though the BBC is unable to verify that figure. It forced PHP Foundation to rush out its announcement of the vulnerability and its huge scale. The Netherlands' National Institute for Public Health and the Environment, an agency of the Dutch government, has taken down its website. Japan's national cyber-security office and EU cyber-security officials have issued a similar warning . "PHP is everywhere. Cyber-security expert Don Smith, from the Sophos Counter Threat Unit, told the BBC this would "likely be a priority target" for hackers. The immediate challenge was not simply installing a patch to fix the issue, but finding and managing every instance where PHP was running, he said. "The use of PHP is pervasive, it can sit beneath public websites, content management systems, hosting platforms and third-party products, sometimes without even being obvious to the organisation using it," he said. He said it was crucial that organisations looked out for signs that an attacker "might have already have gained a foothold". The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said the risk scores given to the vulnerabilities "indicate the potential for unauthenticated remote code execution". Such a cyber-attack could potentially allow hackers to install malware and take down websites. Dane Knecht, chief technology officer at internet infrastructure firm Cloudflare, said he was "seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up". The NCSC said once organisations have installed the update, they should "continuously monitor for security updates from third-party software vendors, including for appliances and services that may bundle PHP".

extraction.body: Cyber security chiefs have warned UK organisations their websites may have to be taken offline, after a researcher using AI discovered a "critical security issue" in a programming language. The Finnish government's website was one of several to be partly disabled because of the incident on Wednesday, along with the websites of several local authorities in the UK. Oxford City Council and the City of Edinburgh Council were among the organisations to take their websites offline, while pages for some BBC programmes were unavailable. The Office for Budget Responsibility said it had followed guidance to take its website offline, "in view of the critical security issues affecting PHP". The security issue identified by the researcher could allow attackers to remotely control any web servers running the widely used programming language, PHP. PHP is used by almost 70% of websites, according cybersecurity firm Cloudflare, and underpins popular platforms such as WordPress and Magento. Organisations have been urged by the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) to update to a new, fixed version of the software. If software cannot be immediately upgraded, organisations should consider taking their websites offline, the NCSC said. The cyber division of the National Security Agency in the US warned weaknesses in the software could provide "a direct path to the server's file system or database". The Wall Street Journal reported that the flaw was discovered in August by Ryan Austin, a researcher at the cybersecurity company Calif, using an advanced AI model developed by OpenAI. PHP developers had reportedly planned a security update on Thursday, but the release was brought forward after details of its work to address the vulnerabilities leaked online. OpenAI, which runs ChatGPT, said in the past two months it has been leading a team of researchers working to address the critical flaw in PHP, and supported its developers as it led the fixes. The company described the incident as "one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory", adding that while AI can help to uncover issues, it can also aid attackers. "To our knowledge, frontier AI found these vulnerabilities before attackers did, opening a defender's window for maintainers and security providers to prepare fixes and protections ahead of disclosure," it said. Former head of the NCSC, Ciaran Martin, told Times Radio the vulnerabilities in PHP had the potential to create a significant loss of personal data. He said: "You're talking about the potential to take the personal details of cards, including those crucial three digits on the back and so forth, so people will want to be on the alert for scams in future. "There's more scope for that. You're talking potentially for ransomware attackers, not to be able to do ransomware directly as a result of this, but to get a foothold into the organisation. "You're talking about easier to impersonate CEOs because you get to know them better. All that sort of scamming and fraud and so forth gets turbocharged."

passages: A judge on Wednesday ordered Meta to pay New Mexico $25 billion after a jury found the company liable for deceiving users about privacy and content moderation policies on Facebook.
Facebook's lawyers argued that the state failed to prove whether people were actually harmed by these deceiving statements.
State prosecutors, though, argued Facebook’s statements deceived the entire population of New Mexico and extended beyond social media users.

Meta attorney Matt Nicholson argued in court that a sum as high as $40 billion would be “shocking to the conscience” while an attorney for New Mexico, Randi McGinn, urged standing up to “tech titans who think they are bulletproof and can do whatever they want.”

The state's case focused on accusations that Facebook deceived users about a data breach stemming from a third-party personality quiz that harvested data from roughly 87 million profiles and sold it to a political consulting firm, Cambridge Analytica, to generate targeted ads.
The now-defunct firm’s clients included the 2016 campaign for President Donald Trump.
New Mexico prosecutors also argued that Facebook allowed misinformation or violent content to proliferate on the platform.
New Mexico was the only state to pursue a trial around the Cambridge Analytica scandal after 48 other states signed a settlement for $18 billion in August.
Lawyers for Meta argued for paying no more than $3.4 billion.
An award 10 times that or even more would violate due process, was unconstitutional and would not hold up under appeal, they said.
Interest on the penalty would accrue during an appeal, but the number of violations Meta is charged with could be reduced.
Representatives for Meta, which previously said it plans to appeal the September verdict, didn't immediately respond to a message seeking comment about the amount.
The Menlo Park, California-based company was scheduled to report its quarterly earnings Wednesday afternoon and its shares were trading 2% higher following the penalty announcement.

extraction.body: See more of our coverage in your search results. A state judge ordered Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta to pay a massive $25 billion penalty for deceiving users about data privacy in connection to the Cambridge Analytica scandal. Wednesday’s bombshell ruling wrapped up a case first brought by New Mexico’s attorney general in 2021 after it was revealed that Cambridge Analytica, a British firm, had improperly harvested the data of up to 87 million Facebook users through a third-party app. New Mexico jurors found on Sept. 25 that Meta had committed more than 43 million violations of state consumer protection laws through misleading statements about the incident – each carrying a penalty of $5,000 per infraction. US District Judge Francis Mathew was tasked with deciding the damages. “Facebook’s wrongdoing — over the course of years and systematically broadcast to the public — goes to the heart of Facebook’s core business practices,” Matthew wrote in a 20-page filing explaining his decision. The case was rooted in 2018 reports from news outlets that found Cambridge Analytica acquired private info about Facebook users without them being aware in order to profile US voters. The $25 billion was just a fraction of what Meta could have been ordered to pay under New Mexico state law – which allowed Judge Matthew to impose a penalty as high as $219 billion. State lawyers had sought a penalty of between $35 billion and $40 billion. During the trial, jurors found that 26 of 29 statements made by Meta and its executives regarding the data leak and related issues were misleading. The judge’s finding is likely to stand up on appeal, according to Vincent Joralemon, Senior Fellow at the Berkeley Center for Law & Technology. “The fact pattern is pretty damning for Meta, and I dont see much to dispute there,” Joralemon told The Post. “The actual damages might get reduced on appeal, but the district court judge did a pretty good job trying to make these as reasonable as possible (and already reduced by something like 90% of the maximum allowable under New Mexico law).” Prior to the judge’s ruling, Meta argued that penalties should be no higher than $3.45 billion – asserting that anything more could cause businesses to flee the state. Meta’s chief legal officer CJ Mahoney reiterated the sentiment on Wednesday, vowing to appeal. “At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online,” he said in a statement. “Meta will continue to build a safe and free platform to connect millions of Americans, grow small businesses, and help the country maintain its competitive edge.” The decision marked another major and costly legal setback for Meta , which is facing thousands of lawsuits in states across the country related to its business practices, data privacy, online safety and social media addiction. New Mexico has been at the forefront of the legal crackdown. In March, a state jury ordered Meta to pay $375 million in civil penalties after determining it misled the public about kids’ safety on its apps and exposed them to online predators. A judge tacked on an additional $567 million in penalties related to that case in August. Elsewhere, Meta agreed in August to a historic $18 billion settlement with a coalition of 48 state attorneys general who accused the company of fueling a teen social media addiction and mental health crisis. As part of that deal, Meta earmarked $459 million cover penalties sought by some of the states related to Cambridge Analytica. Online safety watch Fairplay called New Mexico’s ruling in the Cambridge Analytica case a “landmark penalty.” “Everyone, regardless of their political beliefs, should be horrified by Meta’s reckless disregard of privacy law and its brazen lies about its practices,” Fairplay executive director Josh Golin said in a statement. “Every internal document we’ve seen from Meta demonstrates that the company only cares about its bottom line, so we congratulate New Mexico for hitting the company where it hurts.”

We are confident we will prevail on appeal. In the meantime, Meta will continue to build a safe and free platform to connect millions of Americans, grow small businesses, and help the country maintain its competitive edge,” he added. passages: A judge on Wednesday ordered Meta to pay New Mexico $25 billion after a jury found the company liable for deceiving users about privacy and content moderation policies on Facebook.
Facebook's lawyers argued that the state failed to prove whether people were actually harmed by these deceiving statements.
State prosecutors, though, argued Facebook’s statements deceived the entire population of New Mexico and extended beyond social media users.

Meta attorney Matt Nicholson argued in court that a sum as high as $40 billion would be “shocking to the conscience” while an attorney for New Mexico, Randi McGinn, urged standing up to “tech titans who think they are bulletproof and can do whatever they want.”

The state's case focused on accusations that Facebook deceived users about a data breach stemming from a third-party personality quiz that harvested data from roughly 87 million profiles and sold it to a political consulting firm, Cambridge Analytica, to generate targeted ads.
The now-defunct firm’s clients included the 2016 campaign for President Donald Trump.
New Mexico prosecutors also argued that Facebook allowed misinformation or violent content to proliferate on the platform.
New Mexico was the only state to pursue a trial around the Cambridge Analytica scandal after 48 other states signed a settlement for $18 billion in August.
Lawyers for Meta argued for paying no more than $3.4 billion.
An award 10 times that or even more would violate due process, was unconstitutional and would not hold up under appeal, they said.
Interest on the penalty would accrue during an appeal, but the number of violations Meta is charged with could be reduced.
Representatives for Meta, which previously said it plans to appeal the September verdict, didn't immediately respond to a message seeking comment about the amount.
The Menlo Park, California-based company was scheduled to report its quarterly earnings Wednesday afternoon and its shares were trading 2% higher following the penalty announcement.

Judge Francis Mathew handed down the amount, which state Attorney General Raúl Torrez described as "one of the largest, if not the single largest state verdict against a company in American history.” Representatives for Meta, which previously said it plans to appeal the September verdict, didn't immediately respond to a message seeking comment about the amount. The Menlo Park, California-based company was scheduled to report its quarterly earnings Wednesday afternoon and its shares were trading 2% higher following the penalty announcement. Jurors in September found Meta liable for over 43 million violations of New Mexico consumer protection laws when a political consulting firm, Cambridge Analytica, harvested Facebook user data to generate targeted political ads for the 2016 election. Forty-eight other states settled with Facebook in a nationwide case, but New Mexico chose to take the social media company to court on its own. Attorneys for New Mexico had sought $35 billion to $40 billion, arguing that the company would only change its ways with a sum that affected its stock price. Lawyers for Meta argued for paying no more than $3.4 billion. An award 10 times that or even more would violate due process, was unconstitutional and would not hold up under appeal, they said. Meta argued the state failed to prove misleading statements about privacy and that content moderation actually harmed New Mexicans. Interest on the penalty would accrue during an appeal, but the number of violations Meta is charged with could be reduced. sources.title: Meta slapped with $25B penalty in Cambridge Analytica case in New Mexico, latest legal setback for tech giant - New York Post
passages: New Mexico has been at the forefront of the legal crackdown.
In March, a state jury ordered Meta to pay $375 million in civil penalties after determining it misled the public about kids’ safety on its apps and exposed them to online predators.
A judge tacked on an additional $567 million in penalties related to that case in August.

Wednesday’s bombshell ruling wrapped up a case first brought by New Mexico’s attorney general in 2021 after it was revealed that Cambridge Analytica, a British firm, had improperly harvested the data of up to 87 million Facebook users through a third-party app.

Elsewhere, Meta agreed in August to a historic $18 billion settlement with a coalition of 48 state attorneys general who accused the company of fueling a teen social media addiction and mental health crisis.
As part of that deal, Meta earmarked $459 million cover penalties sought by some of the states related to Cambridge Analytica.

US District Judge Francis Mathew was tasked with deciding the damages.
The $25 billion was just a fraction of what Meta could have been ordered to pay under New Mexico state law – which allowed Judge Matthew to impose a penalty as high as $219 billion.
“Every internal document we’ve seen from Meta demonstrates that the company only cares about its bottom line, so we congratulate New Mexico for hitting the company where it hurts.”
Prior to the judge’s ruling, Meta argued that penalties should be no higher than $3.45 billion – asserting that anything more could cause businesses to flee the state.
During the trial, jurors found that 26 of 29 statements made by Meta and its executives regarding the data leak and related issues were misleading.
“The fact pattern is pretty damning for Meta, and I dont see much to dispute there,” Joralemon told The Post.
Meta’s chief legal officer CJ Mahoney reiterated the sentiment on Wednesday, vowing to appeal.
“Meta will continue to build a safe and free platform to connect millions of Americans, grow small businesses, and help the country maintain its competitive edge.”

extraction.body: See more of our coverage in your search results. A state judge ordered Mark Zuckerberg’s Meta to pay a massive $25 billion penalty for deceiving users about data privacy in connection to the Cambridge Analytica scandal. Wednesday’s bombshell ruling wrapped up a case first brought by New Mexico’s attorney general in 2021 after it was revealed that Cambridge Analytica, a British firm, had improperly harvested the data of up to 87 million Facebook users through a third-party app. New Mexico jurors found on Sept. 25 that Meta had committed more than 43 million violations of state consumer protection laws through misleading statements about the incident – each carrying a penalty of $5,000 per infraction. US District Judge Francis Mathew was tasked with deciding the damages. “Facebook’s wrongdoing — over the course of years and systematically broadcast to the public — goes to the heart of Facebook’s core business practices,” Matthew wrote in a 20-page filing explaining his decision. The case was rooted in 2018 reports from news outlets that found Cambridge Analytica acquired private info about Facebook users without them being aware in order to profile US voters. The $25 billion was just a fraction of what Meta could have been ordered to pay under New Mexico state law – which allowed Judge Matthew to impose a penalty as high as $219 billion. State lawyers had sought a penalty of between $35 billion and $40 billion. During the trial, jurors found that 26 of 29 statements made by Meta and its executives regarding the data leak and related issues were misleading. The judge’s finding is likely to stand up on appeal, according to Vincent Joralemon, Senior Fellow at the Berkeley Center for Law & Technology. “The fact pattern is pretty damning for Meta, and I dont see much to dispute there,” Joralemon told The Post. “The actual damages might get reduced on appeal, but the district court judge did a pretty good job trying to make these as reasonable as possible (and already reduced by something like 90% of the maximum allowable under New Mexico law).” Prior to the judge’s ruling, Meta argued that penalties should be no higher than $3.45 billion – asserting that anything more could cause businesses to flee the state. Meta’s chief legal officer CJ Mahoney reiterated the sentiment on Wednesday, vowing to appeal. “At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online,” he said in a statement. “Meta will continue to build a safe and free platform to connect millions of Americans, grow small businesses, and help the country maintain its competitive edge.” The decision marked another major and costly legal setback for Meta , which is facing thousands of lawsuits in states across the country related to its business practices, data privacy, online safety and social media addiction. New Mexico has been at the forefront of the legal crackdown. In March, a state jury ordered Meta to pay $375 million in civil penalties after determining it misled the public about kids’ safety on its apps and exposed them to online predators. A judge tacked on an additional $567 million in penalties related to that case in August. Elsewhere, Meta agreed in August to a historic $18 billion settlement with a coalition of 48 state attorneys general who accused the company of fueling a teen social media addiction and mental health crisis. As part of that deal, Meta earmarked $459 million cover penalties sought by some of the states related to Cambridge Analytica. Online safety watch Fairplay called New Mexico’s ruling in the Cambridge Analytica case a “landmark penalty.” “Everyone, regardless of their political beliefs, should be horrified by Meta’s reckless disregard of privacy law and its brazen lies about its practices,” Fairplay executive director Josh Golin said in a statement. “Every internal document we’ve seen from Meta demonstrates that the company only cares about its bottom line, so we congratulate New Mexico for hitting the company where it hurts.”

passages: Beyond shopping, Zuckerberg said other popular uses for Muse include personal productivity tasks, such as connecting the AI agent to users’ email or calendars.
The exec stressed that this indicates users trusted Muse’s security setup, which includes a feature called “Muse Secure VM” designed to protect their data and privacy.

Remarkably, the tech company is forecasting that Muse will eventually bring in more revenue per user than its “family of apps” users do today — meaning its users on Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger.
Currently, that figure is around “several hundreds of dollars annually,” Zuckerberg said.

Meta said during its third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday that its AI app Muse has been adopted by more than 10 million users, confirming estimates released earlier this week by market intelligence firm Sensor Tower.
Meta has said it ultimately intends to monetize Muse by keeping it free for most users, but keeping a percentage of the commerce taking place on the platform.
