sources.title: [Meta Platforms Q3 2026 Earnings Call] Meta's 26% Revenue Surge to $64.6 Billion Overshadowed by $9.9 Billion Legal Charge as Muse Personal AI Agent Signs 10 Million Users in Six Weeks - BigGo Finance
passages: Meta Platforms delivered a robust third quarter of 2026, posting revenue of $64.6 billion, up 26% year-over-year on both a reported and constant-currency basis, as advertising demand and user engagement remained strong.

But the headline number was swiftly overshadowed by a $9.9 billion legal charge tied to an August 2026 multi-state attorneys general agreement, which dragged GAAP operating income down 37% to $13 billion and compressed the operating margin to 20%.
The quarter's defining development was not a financial line item but a product launch.
Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, has exploded out of the gate.

More than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada set up Muse agents in roughly six weeks, and about 25% of those users engage with it daily—more than double the early retention rate of Threads, according to CEO Mark Zuckerberg.
Full-year 2026 expenses are now expected at $175 billion-$179 billion , raised to incorporate the legal charge.
CapEx for 2026 is expected at $135 billion-$145 billion, narrowed from the prior $130 billion-$145 billion range.
The tax rate for the quarter came in at 24%, above the company's outlook range, primarily due to the non-deductible portion of legal expenses.
"Growth continues to be strong, and we have been number one in the App Store almost every day."
The Meta AI Business Assistant is also gaining traction.
Advertisers who adopted its recommendations drove almost 5% more conversions at the same cost per conversion and increased their advertising investment by 9% compared with non-adopters.
Nearly 10 million advertisers used at least one of Meta's generative AI tools in Q3, and video generation adoption grew 25% quarter-over-quarter.
Meta's Family of Apps is now used by 3.64 billion people daily .
On the enterprise opportunity, Li said AI is disrupting the enterprise market and incumbents are not entrenched.

"We have differentiated assets to serve this market, bringing together models, infrastructure, global distribution, and long-standing relationships with businesses," she said, citing 500 million businesses already using Meta's products.
She described the enterprise effort as a potential "new diversified, recurring revenue stream" that will develop over multiple years.
Reality Labs revenue slipped 6% to $443 million on lower Quest headset sales, partially offset by strong growth in AI glasses revenue.
The segment posted a loss of $18 billion-$19 billion for 2026, but management expects that to narrow to around $15 billion in 2027 as investment is reallocated toward AI.
On whether Muse will follow Meta's historical playbook of scaling users before monetization, Zuckerberg said monetization will likely come sooner than usual.
"The size of the numbers that we are talking about in terms of both the costs and the opportunity, I think make it important to make progress on that in order to be able to scale it," he said.
Asked about friction with aggregators and suppliers that may resist agentic commerce, Zuckerberg said businesses are "overwhelmingly excited" about the opportunity, though adoption will vary.
Li added that the market will evolve from agents navigating experiences like humans toward permissioned, structured interactions.
Meta has previewed its Personal Agent Protocol with partners including Sierra, Walmart, Stripe, and Shopify.
Muse is coming to Meta Glasses starting next month, which Zuckerberg described as "an important step" toward making personal superintelligence the most important part of the glasses experience.
He also noted that Meta is slowing its VR device cadence to focus on delivering personal superintelligence first.

"We expect to continue investing aggressively to support both our core business and emerging AI initiatives," she said, adding that AI investments position Meta to "sustain strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027."
The most common use case is shopping, with more than a quarter of weekly active users engaging in commerce at an average purchase size above $200.

The company is building capacity to serve more than 1 billion people over the next few years, but Zuckerberg acknowledged that Muse is currently "very compute-intensive to run." extraction.body: Meta Platforms delivered a robust third quarter of 2026, posting revenue of $64.6 billion, up 26% year-over-year on both a reported and constant-currency basis, as advertising demand and user engagement remained strong. But the headline number was swiftly overshadowed by a $9.9 billion legal charge tied to an August 2026 multi-state attorneys general agreement, which dragged GAAP operating income down 37% to $13 billion and compressed the operating margin to 20%. "Excluding the Q3 legal charges related to the aforementioned legal settlement, our third quarter operating income would have increased 11% year-over-year," CFO Susan Li told analysts on the call. The tax rate for the quarter came in at 24%, above the company's outlook range, primarily due to the non-deductible portion of legal expenses. Net income was $9.9 billion, or $3.83 per diluted share. Ad impressions rose 10% year-over-year, healthy across all regions, while the average price per ad increased 14%, driven by ad performance gains and modestly improved macro conditions relative to the year-ago period. Those gains were partially offset by strong impression growth from lower-monetizing surfaces and regions. The quarter's defining development was not a financial line item but a product launch. Muse, Meta's personal AI agent, has exploded out of the gate. More than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada set up Muse agents in roughly six weeks, and about 25% of those users engage with it daily—more than double the early retention rate of Threads, according to CEO Mark Zuckerberg. "In just a month and a half, more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada have set up Muse personal agents," Zuckerberg said. "Growth continues to be strong, and we have been number one in the App Store almost every day." The most common use case is shopping, with more than a quarter of weekly active users engaging in commerce at an average purchase size above $200. Zuckerberg noted that Plaid, a financial data network, "hadn't seen activity like they're seeing with their connector on any other service before," and that Meta had to work with Stripe to raise credit limits in the first week due to unexpectedly high volumes. Meta outlined a multi-pronged monetization strategy: The company is building capacity to serve more than 1 billion people over the next few years, but Zuckerberg acknowledged that Muse is currently "very compute-intensive to run." He expects cost efficiency to improve by more than 10x over the next year , enabling profitability once revenue lines scale. "In the near term, the strength of our core business enables us to scale the Muse network before then, and we believe that we are the best-positioned company to pursue this strategy," Zuckerberg said. Meta's Family of Apps is now used by 3.64 billion people daily . Instagram global time spent per user reached an all-time high, growing double digits year-over-year, with strength across both Reels and Feed. Facebook Reels time spent also hit all-time records globally and in the U.S. Threads continued to scale, with time spent per user growing over 20% year-over-year—and Threads has now overtaken X in monthly active users. The company's AI investments are delivering measurable returns in advertising. Meta Generative Recommender, which uses LLMs to predict the best ad for each user, drove a nearly 2% increase in conversions on Facebook Feed. The GEM ads ranking model expansion added a 1.7% increase in conversions for off-site campaigns and a 9.6% increase for app ads. Andromeda improvements contributed a 1.4% conversion lift on Facebook. The Meta AI Business Assistant is also gaining traction. Advertisers who adopted its recommendations drove almost 5% more conversions at the same cost per conversion and increased their advertising investment by 9% compared with non-adopters. Nearly 10 million advertisers used at least one of Meta's generative AI tools in Q3, and video generation adoption grew 25% quarter-over-quarter. Partnership ads—which allow advertisers to run ads with creators—grew over 97% year-over-year and surpassed a $15 billion annual revenue run rate . The company also completed the global rollout of its Creator Marketing Hub, with more than 10 million creators now discoverable. Reality Labs revenue slipped 6% to $443 million on lower Quest headset sales, partially offset by strong growth in AI glasses revenue. The segment posted a loss of $18 billion-$19 billion for 2026, but management expects that to narrow to around $15 billion in 2027 as investment is reallocated toward AI. Muse is coming to Meta Glasses starting next month, which Zuckerberg described as "an important step" toward making personal superintelligence the most important part of the glasses experience. He also noted that Meta is slowing its VR device cadence to focus on delivering personal superintelligence first. For the fourth quarter, Meta guided total revenue to $73 billion-$76 billion , assuming foreign currency is an approximately 1% headwind to year-over-year growth. Full-year 2026 expenses are now expected at $175 billion-$179 billion , raised to incorporate the legal charge. CapEx for 2026 is expected at $135 billion-$145 billion, narrowed from the prior $130 billion-$145 billion range. The company also announced plans to create a new class of non-voting stock to be distributed through a stock dividend, with stockholders receiving one share of the new non-voting stock for each existing share held—effectively a two-for-one stock split . Trading is expected to begin in late January 2027. Li said the share class is intended for capital raising, employee compensation, acquisitions, and other corporate purposes while preserving the voting power of existing Class A and B shareholders. "We believe the share class will maintain our founder-led structure," she said, adding that there are no specific financing plans to announce at this time. Analysts pressed management on the cost structure of Muse and the company's ability to scale the business profitably. On whether Muse will follow Meta's historical playbook of scaling users before monetization, Zuckerberg said monetization will likely come sooner than usual. "The size of the numbers that we are talking about in terms of both the costs and the opportunity, I think make it important to make progress on that in order to be able to scale it," he said. Asked about friction with aggregators and suppliers that may resist agentic commerce, Zuckerberg said businesses are "overwhelmingly excited" about the opportunity, though adoption will vary. Li added that the market will evolve from agents navigating experiences like humans toward permissioned, structured interactions. Meta has previewed its Personal Agent Protocol with partners including Sierra, Walmart, Stripe, and Shopify. On the enterprise opportunity, Li said AI is disrupting the enterprise market and incumbents are not entrenched. "We have differentiated assets to serve this market, bringing together models, infrastructure, global distribution, and long-standing relationships with businesses," she said, citing 500 million businesses already using Meta's products. She described the enterprise effort as a potential "new diversified, recurring revenue stream" that will develop over multiple years. When pressed for specifics on Muse's per-user cost structure, Li declined to share numbers but outlined near-term efficiency levers including off-peak capacity utilization, smaller models for some tasks, inference optimization, and higher GPU utilization. "Over the longer term, we expect that we are going to be able to, over time, as LLM scale, get more tasks done with fewer tokens," she said. On the 2027 outlook, Li said the company is early in developing its budget and capacity plans but remains committed to investing aggressively. "We expect to continue investing aggressively to support both our core business and emerging AI initiatives," she said, adding that AI investments position Meta to "sustain strong overall revenue growth throughout 2027." According to the Meta chief executive, more than a quarter of Muse users have made purchases through the application, with the average transaction exceeding $200. The figures suggest that the platform is gaining traction not only as a personal AI assistant but also as a potential driver of online commerce, offering Meta another avenue to generate revenue from its expanding AI services. Investors responded positively to the company’s AI developments, with Meta’s shares rising by five per cent in after-hours trading on Wednesday. Muse, which Meta says can assist users with everyday tasks such as sending emails and booking travel, quickly climbed to the top of Apple’s App Store rankings following its release. Its early performance represents an encouraging development for Zuckerberg as the company commits substantial resources to developing AI-powered products and services. At Meta’s annual Connect event, Zuckerberg indicated that the company intended to monetise Muse by collecting a small commission from transactions conducted through the application. “We expect to make money from Muse by taking a small fee from transactions,” Zuckerberg said at the event. The proposed model would allow Meta to earn revenue when users purchase products or services through the app, potentially creating a new commercial opportunity beyond the advertising business that has traditionally driven the company’s earnings. However, the app’s rapid adoption has also brought renewed attention to concerns about consumer trust and the handling of personal information, particularly given the extent of access an AI assistant may require to perform tasks effectively. Kate Winick, a principal analyst at Forrester, identified consumer confidence as a critical factor that could influence the long-term success of Meta’s AI ambitions. “The more information Muse has, the more effective it can be, and overall trust in Meta remains low,” Winick said. She argued that Meta had developed a business model in which users continued engaging with its products despite persistent concerns about data privacy, provided the services delivered sufficient convenience and value. “But Meta has cultivated a reputation that negates trust as a condition for engagement: consumers almost expect to have their data mismanaged in exchange for a high level of connectivity and utility, and have shown that they're willing to keep showing up as long as the product experience delivers,” she added. Winick’s remarks underscore the challenge facing Meta as it expands AI services that may depend on access to personal preferences, communications and other information to deliver useful, tailored responses. The company’s ability to persuade users to trust Muse with such information could prove important as it seeks to turn the application’s early popularity into sustained engagement and commercial growth. The developments also come amid renewed scrutiny of Meta’s data protection practices. Earlier on Wednesday, a judge in New Mexico ordered the company to pay $25 billion after a jury found that it had misled consumers about its handling of personal data and failed to adequately address misinformation on Facebook. The judgment adds to the legal challenges facing the technology company over its treatment of user information, even as it promotes new AI products designed to provide more personalised digital experiences. “The more information Muse has, the more effective it can be, and overall trust in Meta remains low,” Winick said.

She argued that Meta had developed a business model in which users continued engaging with its products despite persistent concerns about data privacy, provided the services delivered sufficient convenience and value.

The developments also come amid renewed scrutiny of Meta’s data protection practices. The judgment adds to the legal challenges facing the technology company over its treatment of user information, even as it promotes new AI products designed to provide more personalised digital experiences.

For Zuckerberg, the app’s growing user base and shopping activity represent an early opportunity to demonstrate the commercial potential of Meta’s AI investments, although its longer-term prospects will depend on whether users continue to find the service useful and are comfortable entrusting it with more of their digital lives.

extraction.body: Two bugs found with AI are behind major issues today for 4chan, DeviantArt, Wikipedia, and the blog where the bar around the corner posts pictures of people’s dogs. The “critical vulnerabilities” were discovered in the PHP programming language, which underpins much of the internet, including any site built on WordPress. Some Dutch and Finnish government agencies took their sites down as a precaution. The NSA Cybersecurity account on X recommended that organizations take their systems offline if “an immediate update is not feasible,” as did the UK’s National Cyber Security Center. It’s been present in PHP for roughly 20 years, but exploiting it “required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve,” according to security firm Wiz. However, powerful AI models have made it much easier to turn that kind of obscure bug into dangerous vulnerabilities. As a casual internet user, you might be wondering what exactly the barrage of jargon like “RCE via OOM corruption” means, how concerned you should be, and how exactly a vulnerability this severe flew under the radar for so long. W3Techs, a survey service, says that the PHP programming language is used by “69.3 percent of all the websites whose server-side programming language we know,” including popular sites like Wikipedia and WordPress. The internet security site VirusTotal says its scanner currently registers about 3.8 million sites running PHP with at least one port open. According to OpenAI, an AI security group called Calif identified a “critical” PHP flaw using GPT-5.6 Sol, and Google-owned Wiz independently discovered and reported the vulnerabilities using AI. The PHP Foundation says that an exploit for one of the vulnerabilities “was theorized” in 2024, but “no concrete vectors were found and other concrete issues with clear impact overshadowed these concerns.” Now the PHP Group says hackers could use the two vulnerabilities for “unauthenticated remote code execution,” like running their own code, changing content, and accessing a site’s stored data without needing an administrator login or password. > RCE via OOM corruption, CVE-2026-109618 (GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w): out-of-memory handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid. > RCE via stale global state, CVE-2026-109619 (GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp): request-owned internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it. The PHP Group says that basically any site running PHP is at risk. OpenAI, which was involved in the vulnerability research, said: “We consider this one of the most impactful security issues in recent memory.” And Wiz said it’s “among the most severe vulnerabilities discovered … in software history.” Last night, the CTO of Cloudflare said that it was “seeing early attacks emerging.” It’s hard to understate just how bad this could get. That includes gaining access to passwords, API keys, cryptographic certificates, and databases of sensitive information. They could also execute code on those servers, turning them into vectors to attack other vulnerable servers. And, thanks to AI, it’s relatively trivial for a determined hacker to exploit these flaws now that they have been revealed. The vulnerability affects servers running PHP and doesn’t necessarily target users directly, but it could use compromised sites to spread malware and steal other valuable data. If you’re feeling extra cautious, check the social accounts of sites and services you frequently use to see if they’ve posted any updates before visiting. If you have a website, even a simple blog, it’s time to check what version of PHP your site uses, if any. GoDaddy says that any site using PHP should assume it is affected and update to the fixed release as soon as possible. It also says that sites running PHP 8.1 or older should upgrade to a newer version, as they’re no longer supported and there will not be an official fix coming. Those on a managed hosting service should check with their provider to see when they should expect the fix to be deployed. If you sell products or services or have any sensitive data on your servers at all, it’s best to disable your site until your host patches their version of PHP.

Developers behind the widely used PHP programming language on Wednesday announced they would issue patches for two critical vulnerabilities, prompting warnings from EU cybersecurity officials that organisations unable to apply the updates should take affected websites offline. Because PHP underpins expansive sections of the internet, concerns have grown over the past day that sites using the software remain vulnerable to severe cyber intrusions. In a blog post, cybersecurity firm Huntress said: "PHP is everywhere. It quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood." PHP confirmed in a security advisory that both security flaws were rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 severity scale, urging users to "upgrade as soon as the release is available". A fix addressing both issues was scheduled to go live at 2pm GMT (3pm BST) on Wednesday. Dane Knecht, the chief technology officer of Web and cloud security firm Cloudflare , said that attacks were emerging and Cloudflare was updating its firewall rules as a stopgap measure. "We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up. This is a STOPGAP only. Patch as soon as PHP releases the update," he said on X. The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said on Tuesday in an advisory that the 9.2 rating indicated a risk of unauthenticated remote code execution, a type of flaw that can allow attackers to run malicious code on vulnerable systems without logging in. CERT-EU urged organisations to prepare for the immediate patching of affected assets and said those unable to do so should consider taking affected sites offline. The Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) issued similar guidance, urging organisations to identify PHP systems in their environments, prepare to apply patches and monitor applications for signs of malicious activity. "ACSC is currently not aware of active exploitation related to these vulnerabilities," the agency said. Web hosting provider GoDaddy said the flaws could allow attackers to execute code on affected servers over the internet, potentially leading to data theft, website defacement or full system compromise. Wordfence, a security plugin that protects WordPress websites, said all WordPress sites run on a PHP-installed server. It warned that automatic updates would not apply the fix and advised site owners to find out who is responsible for updating PHP on their sites. PHP's security team said details of the vulnerabilities, affected versions and the fixed releases would be published when patches are issued. CERT-EU and the ACSC said all PHP versions from PHP 5 onward could be affected, although PHP has not disclosed which versions are vulnerable. extraction.body: PHP Panic: Two Critical Bugs Put 70% of the Internet at Risk, and Everyone Is Freaking Out If you’ve been online at all today, you’ve seen the panic: a critical vulnerability is threatening to “pwn” just about every website on the planet. Finland just started unplugging government websites on Wednesday, the NSA is recommending all organizations using PHP to shut down their sites, and the Netherlands and France did the same. And no, it wasn't a cyberwar. The culprit was PHP, a programming language most people have never heard of. You've almost certainly used it today, though: it runs about 70% of all websites whose server-side language is known, according to W3Techs . PHP is the software working behind the curtain on a website's server—the computer that stores the site and builds each page you ask for. Every WordPress site, for example, sits on a PHP server, per WordPress security firm Wordfence . Two newly found bugs in PHP itself let a stranger run their own commands on that server without ever logging in. Security people call this unauthenticated remote code execution. Everyone else can call it "someone else is driving now." If that server stores your account, your address, or your order history, well, that's theirs too. Web host GoDaddy warned the flaws could let attackers steal data, deface sites, or take over servers entirely. “A flaw like this could let an attacker run their own code on an affected server over the internet, which can lead to stolen data, a defaced site, or a full takeover,” Godaddy says . The PHP Foundation, the nonprofit that funds the language's development, raised the alarm on Tuesday. In a statement shared on X, it said : "The PHP security team is giving advance notice: Upcoming security release Wed, Oct 21st 2026, 14:00UTC, two critical vulnerabilities, both rated CVSSv4 9.2. PHP users are encouraged to prepare to update. Earlier release if details become public or active exploit evidence." The PHP security team is giving advance notice: Upcoming security release Wed, Oct 21st 2026, 14:00UTC, two critical vulnerabilities, both rated CVSSv4 9.2. PHP users are encouraged to prepare to update. Earlier release if details become public or active exploit evidence. That 9.2 comes from CVSS , the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, which grades how dangerous a bug is based on things like how easily it can be reached over the internet and how much damage it can do. It runs from 0 to 10, and anything from 9.0 up is labeled critical—so these two are about as bad as it gets without hitting a perfect 10. The fix landed at roughly 13:35 UTC on Wednesday, a few minutes early, as PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. The security advisory didn't bother being subtle: "All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately." But releasing a fix and having everybody implement the solution are not the same thing, so caution is advised. The first bug, CVE-2026-109618 , shows up when PHP runs out of memory halfway through handling a request, then later treats that half-built data as if it were finished. The second, CVE-2026-109619 , lets leftovers from one visitor's request linger in memory after they should have been tossed, where the next request can trip over them. Think of a cook who keeps reading orders from tickets that are already in the trash. Slip a fake ticket into the bin, and the cook makes whatever you wrote on it. In this case, the “order” is the attacker’s code, and the server runs it. PHP said the risk is highest on servers using a common Apache setup called mod_php, where a demonstrated exploit works "before any application code runs." In other words, the website's own defenses, like login screens and WordPress security plugins, never even wake up. PHP foundation researchers pointed at PHP's upload-progress feature, the thing that tracks how much of a file you've sent, as one of the confirmed ways in. It has been switched on by default for more than a decade, and few websites actually use it. Finland's state IT center, Valtori, began taking public web services offline as a precaution, public broadcaster Yle reported , while the Dutch national cybersecurity agency took down its own website. France's Interior Ministry said its prefecture websites were "temporarily taken offline pending the release of a security patch by the framework's publisher." CERT-EU , the EU's cyber emergency team, told organizations that couldn't patch to "consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is available." That's bureaucrat-speak for "unplug it." Agencies in Australia, Japan, and the U.K. said much the same, according to Reuters . Viral threads on X claimed PHP versions "dating back to 2004" were vulnerable. That traces back to early estimates that everything since PHP 5 was affected, which CERT-EU admitted is based on social media posts. E-commerce security firm Sansec puts the range at PHP 5.4 and later. So 2012, not 2004—still plenty old. PHP only ships official releases for versions 8.2 and newer, which makes the "no fix for old versions" claim half right. Given how bad this one is, its security team also published bare-bones source-code patches for 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1, and Linux distributions are backporting fixes of their own. Security firm Mallory counted about 884,000 internet-facing hosts advertising PHP 8.1 or older on October 20, or 59% of the roughly 1.5 million that publicly show a version. A single shared-hosting server can carry many websites, so the number of sites behind them is higher. Some threads also lumped in Node.js, a different web technology that happened to schedule its own, unrelated security update for the same day. Bad timing. You shouldn’t panic, but also shouldn’t shrug it off. A hacked website, for example, doesn't need to touch a blockchain to empty your wallet. In 2024, attackers redirected the front ends of DeFi protocols Compound and Celer to pages that drained connected wallets, and Curve Finance suffered a similar attack in 2025. I pre-emptively disconnected ALL my sites / VPS servers from the web Those were DNS hijacks, not PHP bugs, but the trick is the same: the site looks right, the URL looks right, and the "approve" button sends your tokens somewhere else. A compromised server can serve exactly that kind of page. Hackers can get very creative, very fast, when it comes to zero-day exploits. Bugs like these are also getting easier to find, with frontier AI models increasingly used to find software vulnerabilities , and experts told Decrypt in June that many more vulnerabilities could surface as those tools spread. Once a patch is public, attackers can compare the old and new code to see exactly what was fixed, and the forensics team at cybersecurity firm Sansec said it expects "mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release." When a different PHP flaw went public in June 2024, Akamai experienced exploit attempts against its decoy servers within 24 hours . So should the average person panic? Not exactly. Your phone, browser, and laptop don't need a PHP patch; the work falls on whoever runs the websites you use. If you run a site, ask your hosting provider whether PHP has been updated, and don't count on WordPress to do it for you: Wordfence warned that automatic updates won't apply this fix and told site owners to find out who is responsible for updating PHP on their servers. Anyone on 8.1 or older needs to plan an upgrade. "The only thing I can say is that the only mitigation is patching / upgrading PHP,” PHP core developer Gina Peter Banyard said on Mastodon . “I sadly know too much." And if you're on PHP 8.2, the fix you just got is one of your last: that version reaches end of life on December 31, 2026, after which it gets no more security patches.

coreStoryFacts.text: The internet security site VirusTotal says its scanner currently registers about 3.8 million sites running PHP with at least one port open.
The “critical vulnerabilities” were discovered in the PHP programming language, which underpins much of the internet, including any site built on WordPress.
The vulnerability affects servers running PHP and doesn’t necessarily target users directly, but it could use compromised sites to spread malware and steal other valuable data.

It’s been present in PHP for roughly 20 years, but exploiting it “required an exceptionally complex chain of steps, at the edge of what human researchers could practically achieve,” according to security firm Wiz.
According to OpenAI, an AI security group called Calif identified a “critical” PHP flaw using GPT-5.6 Sol, and Google-owned Wiz independently discovered and reported the vulnerabilities using AI.
Some Dutch and Finnish government agencies took their sites down as a precaution.
GoDaddy says that any site using PHP should assume it is affected and update to the fixed release as soon as possible.
"ACSC is currently not aware of active exploitation related to these vulnerabilities," the agency said.

Developers behind the widely used PHP programming language on Wednesday announced they would issue patches for two critical vulnerabilities, prompting warnings from EU cybersecurity officials that organisations unable to apply the updates should take affected websites offline.

Web hosting provider GoDaddy said the flaws could allow attackers to execute code on affected servers over the internet, potentially leading to data theft, website defacement or full system compromise.

Finland's public internet web services were being taken offline on Wednesday as a precautionary move against a critical security vulnerability, according to the Government ICT Centre (Valtori), which maintains the sites.
A number of other websites in Finland were taken down, including the site of the Helsinki Book Fair, which is starting on Thursday.
The Finnish Film Foundation (SES) has also announced that its website has been closed.
On Wednesday, the developers of PHP announced they would issue patches for two critical vulnerabilities.

Start your Independent Membership today. Developers behind the widely used PHP programming language on Wednesday announced they would issue patches for two critical vulnerabilities, prompting warnings from EU cybersecurity officials that organisations unable to apply the updates should take affected websites offline. Because PHP underpins expansive sections of the internet, concerns have grown over the past day that sites using the software remain vulnerable to severe cyber intrusions. In a blog post, cybersecurity firm Huntress said: "PHP is everywhere. It quietly powers WordPress, Drupal, Joomla, and Magento sites, shared hosting platforms, control panels, and an awful lot of software that doesn't even advertise that it runs PHP under the hood." PHP confirmed in a security advisory that both security flaws were rated 9.2 on the CVSS v4.0 severity scale, urging users to "upgrade as soon as the release is available". A fix addressing both issues was scheduled to go live at 2pm GMT (3pm BST) on Wednesday. Dane Knecht, the chief technology officer of Web and cloud security firm Cloudflare , said that attacks were emerging and Cloudflare was updating its firewall rules as a stopgap measure. "We are seeing early attacks emerging and are updating mitigations as new vectors show up. This is a STOPGAP only. Patch as soon as PHP releases the update," he said on X. The European Union Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-EU) said on Tuesday in an advisory that the 9.2 rating indicated a risk of unauthenticated remote code execution, a type of flaw that can allow attackers to run malicious code on vulnerable systems without logging in. CERT-EU urged organisations to prepare for the immediate patching of affected assets and said those unable to do so should consider taking affected sites offline. The Australian Cyber Security Centre (ACSC) issued similar guidance, urging organisations to identify PHP systems in their environments, prepare to apply patches and monitor applications for signs of malicious activity. "ACSC is currently not aware of active exploitation related to these vulnerabilities," the agency said. Web hosting provider GoDaddy said the flaws could allow attackers to execute code on affected servers over the internet, potentially leading to data theft, website defacement or full system compromise. Wordfence, a security plugin that protects WordPress websites, said all WordPress sites run on a PHP-installed server. It warned that automatic updates would not apply the fix and advised site owners to find out who is responsible for updating PHP on their sites. PHP's security team said details of the vulnerabilities, affected versions and the fixed releases would be published when patches are issued. CERT-EU and the ACSC said all PHP versions from PHP 5 onward could be affected, although PHP has not disclosed which versions are vulnerable. extraction.body: PHP Panic: Two Critical Bugs Put 70% of the Internet at Risk, and Everyone Is Freaking Out If you’ve been online at all today, you’ve seen the panic: a critical vulnerability is threatening to “pwn” just about every website on the planet. Finland just started unplugging government websites on Wednesday, the NSA is recommending all organizations using PHP to shut down their sites, and the Netherlands and France did the same. And no, it wasn't a cyberwar. The culprit was PHP, a programming language most people have never heard of. You've almost certainly used it today, though: it runs about 70% of all websites whose server-side language is known, according to W3Techs . PHP is the software working behind the curtain on a website's server—the computer that stores the site and builds each page you ask for. Every WordPress site, for example, sits on a PHP server, per WordPress security firm Wordfence . Two newly found bugs in PHP itself let a stranger run their own commands on that server without ever logging in. Security people call this unauthenticated remote code execution. Everyone else can call it "someone else is driving now." If that server stores your account, your address, or your order history, well, that's theirs too. Web host GoDaddy warned the flaws could let attackers steal data, deface sites, or take over servers entirely. “A flaw like this could let an attacker run their own code on an affected server over the internet, which can lead to stolen data, a defaced site, or a full takeover,” Godaddy says . The PHP Foundation, the nonprofit that funds the language's development, raised the alarm on Tuesday. In a statement shared on X, it said : "The PHP security team is giving advance notice: Upcoming security release Wed, Oct 21st 2026, 14:00UTC, two critical vulnerabilities, both rated CVSSv4 9.2. PHP users are encouraged to prepare to update. Earlier release if details become public or active exploit evidence." The PHP security team is giving advance notice: Upcoming security release Wed, Oct 21st 2026, 14:00UTC, two critical vulnerabilities, both rated CVSSv4 9.2. PHP users are encouraged to prepare to update. Earlier release if details become public or active exploit evidence. That 9.2 comes from CVSS , the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, which grades how dangerous a bug is based on things like how easily it can be reached over the internet and how much damage it can do. It runs from 0 to 10, and anything from 9.0 up is labeled critical—so these two are about as bad as it gets without hitting a perfect 10. The fix landed at roughly 13:35 UTC on Wednesday, a few minutes early, as PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. The security advisory didn't bother being subtle: "All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately." But releasing a fix and having everybody implement the solution are not the same thing, so caution is advised. The first bug, CVE-2026-109618 , shows up when PHP runs out of memory halfway through handling a request, then later treats that half-built data as if it were finished. The second, CVE-2026-109619 , lets leftovers from one visitor's request linger in memory after they should have been tossed, where the next request can trip over them. Think of a cook who keeps reading orders from tickets that are already in the trash. Slip a fake ticket into the bin, and the cook makes whatever you wrote on it. In this case, the “order” is the attacker’s code, and the server runs it. PHP said the risk is highest on servers using a common Apache setup called mod_php, where a demonstrated exploit works "before any application code runs." In other words, the website's own defenses, like login screens and WordPress security plugins, never even wake up. PHP foundation researchers pointed at PHP's upload-progress feature, the thing that tracks how much of a file you've sent, as one of the confirmed ways in. It has been switched on by default for more than a decade, and few websites actually use it. Finland's state IT center, Valtori, began taking public web services offline as a precaution, public broadcaster Yle reported , while the Dutch national cybersecurity agency took down its own website. France's Interior Ministry said its prefecture websites were "temporarily taken offline pending the release of a security patch by the framework's publisher." CERT-EU , the EU's cyber emergency team, told organizations that couldn't patch to "consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is available." That's bureaucrat-speak for "unplug it." Agencies in Australia, Japan, and the U.K. said much the same, according to Reuters . Viral threads on X claimed PHP versions "dating back to 2004" were vulnerable. That traces back to early estimates that everything since PHP 5 was affected, which CERT-EU admitted is based on social media posts. E-commerce security firm Sansec puts the range at PHP 5.4 and later. So 2012, not 2004—still plenty old. PHP only ships official releases for versions 8.2 and newer, which makes the "no fix for old versions" claim half right. Given how bad this one is, its security team also published bare-bones source-code patches for 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1, and Linux distributions are backporting fixes of their own. Security firm Mallory counted about 884,000 internet-facing hosts advertising PHP 8.1 or older on October 20, or 59% of the roughly 1.5 million that publicly show a version. A single shared-hosting server can carry many websites, so the number of sites behind them is higher. Some threads also lumped in Node.js, a different web technology that happened to schedule its own, unrelated security update for the same day. Bad timing. You shouldn’t panic, but also shouldn’t shrug it off. A hacked website, for example, doesn't need to touch a blockchain to empty your wallet. In 2024, attackers redirected the front ends of DeFi protocols Compound and Celer to pages that drained connected wallets, and Curve Finance suffered a similar attack in 2025. I pre-emptively disconnected ALL my sites / VPS servers from the web Those were DNS hijacks, not PHP bugs, but the trick is the same: the site looks right, the URL looks right, and the "approve" button sends your tokens somewhere else. A compromised server can serve exactly that kind of page. Hackers can get very creative, very fast, when it comes to zero-day exploits. Bugs like these are also getting easier to find, with frontier AI models increasingly used to find software vulnerabilities , and experts told Decrypt in June that many more vulnerabilities could surface as those tools spread. Once a patch is public, attackers can compare the old and new code to see exactly what was fixed, and the forensics team at cybersecurity firm Sansec said it expects "mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release." When a different PHP flaw went public in June 2024, Akamai experienced exploit attempts against its decoy servers within 24 hours . So should the average person panic? Not exactly. Your phone, browser, and laptop don't need a PHP patch; the work falls on whoever runs the websites you use. If you run a site, ask your hosting provider whether PHP has been updated, and don't count on WordPress to do it for you: Wordfence warned that automatic updates won't apply this fix and told site owners to find out who is responsible for updating PHP on their servers. Anyone on 8.1 or older needs to plan an upgrade. "The only thing I can say is that the only mitigation is patching / upgrading PHP,” PHP core developer Gina Peter Banyard said on Mastodon . “I sadly know too much." And if you're on PHP 8.2, the fix you just got is one of your last: that version reaches end of life on December 31, 2026, after which it gets no more security patches.

PHP users are encouraged to prepare to update. Earlier release if details become public or active exploit evidence."
The PHP security team is giving advance notice: Upcoming security release Wed, Oct 21st 2026, 14:00UTC, two critical vulnerabilities, both rated CVSSv4 9.2.
PHP users are encouraged to prepare to update. Earlier release if details become public or active exploit evidence.

That 9.2 comes from CVSS , the Common Vulnerability Scoring System, which grades how dangerous a bug is based on things like how easily it can be reached over the internet and how much damage it can do. It runs from 0 to 10, and anything from 9.0 up is labeled critical—so these two are about as bad as it gets without hitting a perfect 10.

The fix landed at roughly 13:35 UTC on Wednesday, a few minutes early, as PHP versions 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35. The security advisory didn't bother being subtle: "All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately."
But releasing a fix and having everybody implement the solution are not the same thing, so caution is advised.

The first bug, CVE-2026-109618 , shows up when PHP runs out of memory halfway through handling a request, then later treats that half-built data as if it were finished. The second, CVE-2026-109619 , lets leftovers from one visitor's request linger in memory after they should have been tossed, where the next request can trip over them.

Think of a cook who keeps reading orders from tickets that are already in the trash. Slip a fake ticket into the bin, and the cook makes whatever you wrote on it. In this case, the “order” is the attacker’s code, and the server runs it.

PHP said the risk is highest on servers using a common Apache setup called mod_php, where a demonstrated exploit works "before any application code runs." In other words, the website's own defenses, like login screens and WordPress security plugins, never even wake up.

PHP foundation researchers pointed at PHP's upload-progress feature, the thing that tracks how much of a file you've sent, as one of the confirmed ways in. It has been switched on by default for more than a decade, and few websites actually use it.

Finland's state IT center, Valtori, began taking public web services offline as a precaution, public broadcaster Yle reported , while the Dutch national cybersecurity agency took down its own website.
France's Interior Ministry said its prefecture websites were "temporarily taken offline pending the release of a security patch by the framework's publisher."

CERT-EU , the EU's cyber emergency team, told organizations that couldn't patch to "consider isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until a fix is available." That's bureaucrat-speak for "unplug it." Agencies in Australia, Japan, and the U.K. said much the same, according to Reuters .

Viral threads on X claimed PHP versions "dating back to 2004" were vulnerable. That traces back to early estimates that everything since PHP 5 was affected, which CERT-EU admitted is based on social media posts.
E-commerce security firm Sansec puts the range at PHP 5.4 and later. So 2012, not 2004—still plenty old.

PHP only ships official releases for versions 8.2 and newer, which makes the "no fix for old versions" claim half right. Given how bad this one is, its security team also published bare-bones source-code patches for 7.4, 8.0, and 8.1, and Linux distributions are backporting fixes of their own.

Security firm Mallory counted about 884,000 internet-facing hosts advertising PHP 8.1 or older on October 20, or 59% of the roughly 1.5 million that publicly show a version. A single shared-hosting server can carry many websites, so the number of sites behind them is higher.
Some threads also lumped in Node.js, a different web technology that happened to schedule its own, unrelated security update for the same day. Bad timing.

You shouldn’t panic, but also shouldn’t shrug it off. A hacked website, for example, doesn't need to touch a blockchain to empty your wallet. In 2024, attackers redirected the front ends of DeFi protocols Compound and Celer to pages that drained connected wallets, and Curve Finance suffered a similar attack in 2025.
I pre-emptively disconnected ALL my sites / VPS servers from the web

Those were DNS hijacks, not PHP bugs, but the trick is the same: the site looks right, the URL looks right, and the "approve" button sends your tokens somewhere else. A compromised server can serve exactly that kind of page.
Hackers can get very creative, very fast, when it comes to zero-day exploits.

Bugs like these are also getting easier to find, with frontier AI models increasingly used to find software vulnerabilities , and experts told Decrypt in June that many more vulnerabilities could surface as those tools spread.

Once a patch is public, attackers can compare the old and new code to see exactly what was fixed, and the forensics team at cybersecurity firm Sansec said it expects "mass attacks to start within 15 minutes of the release." When a different PHP flaw went public in June 2024, Akamai experienced exploit attempts against its decoy servers within 24 hours .
So should the average person panic? Not exactly. Your phone, browser, and laptop don't need a PHP patch; the work falls on whoever runs the websites you use.

If you run a site, ask your hosting provider whether PHP has been updated, and don't count on WordPress to do it for you: Wordfence warned that automatic updates won't apply this fix and told site owners to find out who is responsible for updating PHP on their servers. Anyone on 8.1 or older needs to plan an upgrade.
"The only thing I can say is that the only mitigation is patching / upgrading PHP,” PHP core developer Gina Peter Banyard said on Mastodon . “I sadly know too much."
And if you're on PHP 8.2, the fix you just got is one of your last: that version reaches end of life on December 31, 2026, after which it gets no more security patches.

The culprit was PHP, a programming language most people have never heard of.
You've almost certainly used it today, though: it runs about 70% of all websites whose server-side language is known, according to W3Techs .
If you’ve been online at all today, you’ve seen the panic: a critical vulnerability is threatening to “pwn” just about every website on the planet.
Finland just started unplugging government websites on Wednesday, the NSA is recommending all organizations using PHP to shut down their sites, and the Netherlands and France did the same.

sources.title: Data centers could erase decades of air quality gains
passages: In just five years, it would be enough pollution to wipe out decades of gains in air quality.
sources.body: In just five years, it would be enough pollution to wipe out decades of gains in air quality.

extraction.body: A rush of new data centers could bring air pollution roaring back to levels not seen since the 2000s in Texas, which has become ground zero for the physical infrastructure behind generative AI. New and proposed data centers are demanding a tremendous amount of electricity. How developers and utilities meet that demand — with gas turbines or renewable energy — will determine just how dirty things will get. Tech companies and data center developers are devising new ways to get enough electricity, including building out their own power sources. But if all planned data center projects were to plug into the electricity grid in Texas and be powered by the anticipated grid mix, soot and smog-forming pollutants would skyrocket, according to a new report from the Houston Advanced Research Center (HARC). In just five years, it would be enough pollution to wipe out decades of gains in air quality. In that scenario, fine particle pollution or soot from the power sector would more than triple, reaching its highest level since 2006. Smog-forming NOx emissions would increase 136 percent, approaching pollution levels from 2004. Planet-heating carbon dioxide pollution would climb 90 percent above what they were in 2025. HARC modeled different outcomes based on three different projections for data center energy demand. Many proposed data center projects are speculative and could fall by the wayside. And developers can limit the environmental impact of a data center by building solar and wind farms onsite. NOx emissions could be up to 10 times lower if data centers pair grid power with renewable electricity generated onsite. But if developers decide to build gas engines on site to power their data centers as a way to avoid long wait times to connect to the grid, the opposite could also play out, resulting in the highest pollution levels possible. Data center capacity is typically measured by how much power they draw, and Texas has become the leading data center market in this measure with 26 gigawatts of existing and under-construction capacity. Texas is also bracing for four times more proposed data center capacity running on power generated onsite than any other state, according to a separate Wood Mackenzie report published in March. And in many cases, developers are turning to less efficient gas turbine technology in order to speed construction — another trend that’s making the data center boom more polluting than it needs to be. “There is a good chance that our children and grandchildren will breathe dirtier air than we did,” John Hall, HARC CEO, said in a press release. “The transportation sector, the state, and other stakeholders have been working for decades to successfully bring these [emissions] numbers down, and that progress is now at risk.”

passages: The study notes that does not mean all Texas emissions would rise by 2 to 10 times, but it identifies the choice of power supply as a major factor in the air-quality impact.

A new study from the Houston Advanced Research Center is warning that the rapid growth of data centers could erase much of Texas’ air-quality progress over the past two decades, depending largely on how those facilities are powered.

The study focuses on “criteria pollutants” and models multiple scenarios for how rising electricity demand from the data center industry could affect air pollution across the state, including Central Texas.

"I lost about $70,000 in value on my lower middle-class income home." Last week, Bastrop County residents recently demanded the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality hold a meeting to discuss another company’s project permit.
The TCEQ recently said it would halt permitting for data center developments to fall in line with a September order from Texas Gov.

By operating our own power 'behind-the-meter,' we place zero operational demand on the public electrical grid, fulfilling the state's goal to protect the grid and prevent rising utility costs for Texas families.

extraction.body: A new study from the Houston Advanced Research Center is warning that the rapid growth of data centers could erase much of Texas’ air-quality progress over the past two decades, depending largely on how those facilities are powered. The study focuses on “criteria pollutants” and models multiple scenarios for how rising electricity demand from the data center industry could affect air pollution across the state, including Central Texas. Carlos Gamarra, vice president of Energy, Air and Digital Solutions at the Houston Advanced Research Center and a co-author of the study, said the analysis found that if Texas continues with the current electricity mix, emissions could return to levels last seen decades ago. “By projecting emissions by the current power grid mix, we saw that for multiple criteria pollutants, we will be going back to the emissions levels we had in the 2000s,” said Gamarra. The study estimates nitrogen oxide emissions—which help form ground-level ozone, a key component of smog—could be 2 to 10 times higher if data center demand is met with on-site combustion rather than grid power paired with solar and wind. The study notes that does not mean all Texas emissions would rise by 2 to 10 times, but it identifies the choice of power supply as a major factor in the air-quality impact. Jay Mirabito, who lives in the Elm Ridge subdivision, said he is frustrated by pollution he attributes to construction of a data center campus by developer EdgeConneX. “We're experiencing a lot of noise pollution, a lot [of] like dust drifts and concrete drifts over our neighborhood,” Mirabito said. Mirabito also noted impacts like a dip in property values over the past year, as a correlation to the neighboring centers being built. "Our tax appraisals came back and nearly everybody's lost value," said Mirabito. "I lost about $70,000 in value on my lower middle-class income home." Last week, Bastrop County residents recently demanded the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality hold a meeting to discuss another company’s project permit. Pacifico Energy is planning a natural gas plant to power a data center near residents. HARC forecasts that nitrogen oxide emissions from natural gas could increase by more than 141.5 percent between 2025 and 2031. “We need to pay attention to the evolution of the data center industry and how that affects communities,” said Gamarra. The TCEQ recently said it would halt permitting for data center developments to fall in line with a September order from Texas Gov. CBS Austin reported it reached out to three companies with data center development plans in Central Texas—Pacifico, EdgeConneX and Big Watt + Powerhouse. Big Watt + Powerhouse was the only developer to respond at the time of this report, stating in part that its facility in Taylor will neutralize up to 90 percent or more of nitrogen oxide emissions. Our facility was engineered from the ground up to align with statewide standards established by Governor Abbott. By operating our own power 'behind-the-meter,' we place zero operational demand on the public electrical grid, fulfilling the state's goal to protect the grid and prevent rising utility costs for Texas families. Our facility will integrate advanced Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) technology, which will neutralize up to 90% or more of nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions. The HARC study maps out several different development paths for the state, ranging from unmitigated traditional generation to highly optimized, clean infrastructure scenarios. Gamarra said the goal is to limit the industry’s footprint as it expands. “We want to help minimize the environmental impacts of this industry while it develops,” he said. HARC has a policy playbook designed with what it believes is a roadmap for developers and lawmakers to follow when "managing data center growth."

passages: A new study has tabulated the toll from two decades of wildfires on air quality and human health in the continental U.S.
“Our air is supposed to be cleaner and cleaner due mostly to EPA regulations on emissions, but the fires have limited or erased these air-quality gains,” says Jun Wang , James E.
sources.body: A new study has tabulated the toll from two decades of wildfires on air quality and human health in the continental U.S. “Our air is supposed to be cleaner and cleaner due mostly to EPA regulations on emissions, but the fires have limited or erased these air-quality gains,” says Jun Wang , James E.

extraction.body: You need only to remember last summer’s wildfires in the United States and Canada, which fouled the air from coast to coast, to know the effects these blazes can have on the environment and human health. A new study has tabulated the toll from two decades of wildfires on air quality and human health in the continental U.S. The authors report that from 2000 to 2020, the air has worsened in the western U.S., mainly due to the increase in frequency and ferocity of wildfires causing an increase of 670 premature deaths per year in the region during that time period. Overall, the study’s authors report fires have undercut successful federal efforts to improve air quality primarily through reductions in automobile emissions. “Our air is supposed to be cleaner and cleaner due mostly to EPA regulations on emissions, but the fires have limited or erased these air-quality gains,” says Jun Wang , James E. Ashton professor and chair in the Department of Chemical and Biochemical Engineering and the lead corresponding author on the study. “In other words, all the efforts for the past 20 years by the EPA to make our air cleaner basically have been lost in fire-prone areas and downwind regions. We are losing ground.” The researchers calculated the concentration of black carbon, a fine-particle air pollutant that has been linked to respiratory and heart disease, on a kilometer-by-kilometer (0.6 miles) grid for the continental U.S. In the western U.S., the researchers report black carbon concentrations have risen 86%, on an annual basis, mostly due to wildfires. Not surprisingly, the highest premature mortality rates were in the western U.S., the region where the wildfires originated or that was most affected by smoke from wildfires in Canada. The authors say the increase of 670 premature deaths per year is a conservative estimate, as black carbon’s effects on human health are not fully understood. “Wildfires have become increasingly intensive and frequent in the western U.S., resulting in a significant increase in smoke-related emissions in populated areas,” Wang and his team write. “This has likely contributed to a decline in air quality and an increase in attributable mortality.” The fires also have affected the Midwest. Smoke transported in the atmosphere affects air quality, though direct effects on health appear, for now, to be minimal. But, Wang says, “we are on the borderline. If fires increase or become more frequent, our air quality will get worse.” The eastern U.S. had no major declines in air quality during the 2000-20 time period. The researchers derived black carbon concentrations and premature deaths estimates from satellite data and 500 ground-based stations that monitor air quality. The data from surface stations can be extensive, but it does not give complete spatial coverage and can be lacking in rural areas. So, the researchers employed “deep learning,” which enables computer systems to cluster data and produce accurate predictions, to calculate the black carbon concentrations. They calculated premature deaths through a formula that incorporated average life span, black carbon exposure, and population density. “This is the first time to look at black carbon concentrations everywhere, and at one-kilometer resolution,” Wang says. Jing Wei , the study’s lead author, led the collection of satellite data of fine particulates and the analysis of these pollutants on public health when he was a postdoctoral research scholar in Wang’s research group at Iowa. “The increasing number and intensity of wildfires in the U.S. counteract or even overshadow the reduction in anthropogenic emissions, exacerbating air pollution and heightening the risks of both morbidity and mortality,” says Wei, now assistant research scientist at the University of Maryland’s Earth System Science Interdisciplinary Center. The study, “Long-term mortality burden trends attributed to black carbon and PM2.5 from wildfire emissions across the continental US from 2000-2020: a deep learning modelling study,” was published online Dec. 4 in the journal The Lancet Planetary Health . Zhanqing Li, from the University of Maryland's Earth System Science Interdisciplinary Center, who supervises Wei, is a co-corresponding author. Contributing authors include Shobha Kondragunta, from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration’s STAR Center for Satellite Applications and Research; Susan Anenberg, from George Washington University; Yi Wang and Huanxin Zhang, from Iowa; David Diner, from the California Institute of Technology and NASA Jet Propulsion Lab; Jenny Hand, from Colorado State University; Alexei Lyapustin, Ralph Kahn, Peter Colarco, and Arlindo da Silva, from NASA Goddard Space Flight Center; and Charles Ichoku, from the University of Maryland-Baltimore County.

sources.title: Alberta's data centre plans would erase gains from phasing out coal - Corporate Knights
passages: Celebrity investor Kevin O’Leary’s proposed $70-billion data centre, designed to run on 7.5 gigawatts of gas-fired power, could raise Alberta’s greenhouse gas emissions to levels not seen since the coal era , according to estimates obtained by The Energy Mix .
Another requirement for data centres is the large amount of water they use for cooling.
But water is also needed to run gas power plants.

Even though the Grande Prairie area is known for longer, colder winters, Wang estimated that the water needed for the fully completed data centre, including both cooling and for the power plant, would be between 112 and 195 billion litres per year.
That is roughly one-third to two-thirds of the total annual water consumption of all the households in Alberta.
The reversal would set the province and Canada back about 20 years, matching the 27 megatonnes of coal emissions Alberta phased out between 2005 and 2023.
It has been edited to conform with Corporate Knights style.
Planned in an area battling drought, the project’s water needs would also be vast, rivalling the annual use of hundreds of thousands of Alberta households.

extraction.body: A rush of new data centers could bring air pollution roaring back to levels not seen since the 2000s in Texas, which has become ground zero for the physical infrastructure behind generative AI. New and proposed data centers are demanding a tremendous amount of electricity. How developers and utilities meet that demand — with gas turbines or renewable energy — will determine just how dirty things will get. Tech companies and data center developers are devising new ways to get enough electricity, including building out their own power sources. But if all planned data center projects were to plug into the electricity grid in Texas and be powered by the anticipated grid mix, soot and smog-forming pollutants would skyrocket, according to a new report from the Houston Advanced Research Center (HARC). In just five years, it would be enough pollution to wipe out decades of gains in air quality. In that scenario, fine particle pollution or soot from the power sector would more than triple, reaching its highest level since 2006. Smog-forming NOx emissions would increase 136 percent, approaching pollution levels from 2004. Planet-heating carbon dioxide pollution would climb 90 percent above what they were in 2025. HARC modeled different outcomes based on three different projections for data center energy demand. Many proposed data center projects are speculative and could fall by the wayside. And developers can limit the environmental impact of a data center by building solar and wind farms onsite. NOx emissions could be up to 10 times lower if data centers pair grid power with renewable electricity generated onsite. But if developers decide to build gas engines on site to power their data centers as a way to avoid long wait times to connect to the grid, the opposite could also play out, resulting in the highest pollution levels possible. Data center capacity is typically measured by how much power they draw, and Texas has become the leading data center market in this measure with 26 gigawatts of existing and under-construction capacity. Texas is also bracing for four times more proposed data center capacity running on power generated onsite than any other state, according to a separate Wood Mackenzie report published in March. And in many cases, developers are turning to less efficient gas turbine technology in order to speed construction — another trend that’s making the data center boom more polluting than it needs to be. “There is a good chance that our children and grandchildren will breathe dirtier air than we did,” John Hall, HARC CEO, said in a press release. “The transportation sector, the state, and other stakeholders have been working for decades to successfully bring these [emissions] numbers down, and that progress is now at risk.”

extraction.body: A new study from the Houston Advanced Research Center is warning that the rapid growth of data centers could erase much of Texas’ air-quality progress over the past two decades, depending largely on how those facilities are powered. The study focuses on “criteria pollutants” and models multiple scenarios for how rising electricity demand from the data center industry could affect air pollution across the state, including Central Texas. Carlos Gamarra, vice president of Energy, Air and Digital Solutions at the Houston Advanced Research Center and a co-author of the study, said the analysis found that if Texas continues with the current electricity mix, emissions could return to levels last seen decades ago. “By projecting emissions by the current power grid mix, we saw that for multiple criteria pollutants, we will be going back to the emissions levels we had in the 2000s,” said Gamarra. The study estimates nitrogen oxide emissions—which help form ground-level ozone, a key component of smog—could be 2 to 10 times higher if data center demand is met with on-site combustion rather than grid power paired with solar and wind. The study notes that does not mean all Texas emissions would rise by 2 to 10 times, but it identifies the choice of power supply as a major factor in the air-quality impact. Jay Mirabito, who lives in the Elm Ridge subdivision, said he is frustrated by pollution he attributes to construction of a data center campus by developer EdgeConneX. “We're experiencing a lot of noise pollution, a lot [of] like dust drifts and concrete drifts over our neighborhood,” Mirabito said. Mirabito also noted impacts like a dip in property values over the past year, as a correlation to the neighboring centers being built. "Our tax appraisals came back and nearly everybody's lost value," said Mirabito. "I lost about $70,000 in value on my lower middle-class income home." Last week, Bastrop County residents recently demanded the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality hold a meeting to discuss another company’s project permit. Pacifico Energy is planning a natural gas plant to power a data center near residents. HARC forecasts that nitrogen oxide emissions from natural gas could increase by more than 141.5 percent between 2025 and 2031. “We need to pay attention to the evolution of the data center industry and how that affects communities,” said Gamarra. The TCEQ recently said it would halt permitting for data center developments to fall in line with a September order from Texas Gov. CBS Austin reported it reached out to three companies with data center development plans in Central Texas—Pacifico, EdgeConneX and Big Watt + Powerhouse. Big Watt + Powerhouse was the only developer to respond at the time of this report, stating in part that its facility in Taylor will neutralize up to 90 percent or more of nitrogen oxide emissions. Our facility was engineered from the ground up to align with statewide standards established by Governor Abbott. By operating our own power 'behind-the-meter,' we place zero operational demand on the public electrical grid, fulfilling the state's goal to protect the grid and prevent rising utility costs for Texas families. Our facility will integrate advanced Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) technology, which will neutralize up to 90% or more of nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions. The HARC study maps out several different development paths for the state, ranging from unmitigated traditional generation to highly optimized, clean infrastructure scenarios. Gamarra said the goal is to limit the industry’s footprint as it expands. “We want to help minimize the environmental impacts of this industry while it develops,” he said. HARC has a policy playbook designed with what it believes is a roadmap for developers and lawmakers to follow when "managing data center growth."

Carlos Gamarra, vice president of Energy, Air and Digital Solutions at the Houston Advanced Research Center and a co-author of the study, said the analysis found that if Texas continues with the current electricity mix, emissions could return to levels last seen decades ago. “By projecting emissions by the current power grid mix, we saw that for multiple criteria pollutants, we will be going back to the emissions levels we had in the 2000s,” said Gamarra.

The study estimates nitrogen oxide emissions—which help form ground-level ozone, a key component of smog—could be 2 to 10 times higher if data center demand is met with on-site combustion rather than grid power paired with solar and wind.
The study notes that does not mean all Texas emissions would rise by 2 to 10 times, but it identifies the choice of power supply as a major factor in the air-quality impact.

Jay Mirabito, who lives in the Elm Ridge subdivision, said he is frustrated by pollution he attributes to construction of a data center campus by developer EdgeConneX. “We're experiencing a lot of noise pollution, a lot [of] like dust drifts and concrete drifts over our neighborhood,” Mirabito said.
Mirabito also noted impacts like a dip in property values over the past year, as a correlation to the neighboring centers being built.
"Our tax appraisals came back and nearly everybody's lost value," said Mirabito.

"I lost about $70,000 in value on my lower middle-class income home." Last week, Bastrop County residents recently demanded the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality hold a meeting to discuss another company’s project permit.
Pacifico Energy is planning a natural gas plant to power a data center near residents.

HARC forecasts that nitrogen oxide emissions from natural gas could increase by more than 141.5 percent between 2025 and 2031. “We need to pay attention to the evolution of the data center industry and how that affects communities,” said Gamarra.
The TCEQ recently said it would halt permitting for data center developments to fall in line with a September order from Texas Gov.
CBS Austin reported it reached out to three companies with data center development plans in Central Texas—Pacifico, EdgeConneX and Big Watt + Powerhouse.
Big Watt + Powerhouse was the only developer to respond at the time of this report, stating in part that its facility in Taylor will neutralize up to 90 percent or more of nitrogen oxide emissions.
Our facility was engineered from the ground up to align with statewide standards established by Governor Abbott.

By operating our own power 'behind-the-meter,' we place zero operational demand on the public electrical grid, fulfilling the state's goal to protect the grid and prevent rising utility costs for Texas families.
Our facility will integrate advanced Selective Catalytic Reduction (SCR) technology, which will neutralize up to 90% or more of nitrogen oxide (NOx) emissions.
The HARC study maps out several different development paths for the state, ranging from unmitigated traditional generation to highly optimized, clean infrastructure scenarios.
Gamarra said the goal is to limit the industry’s footprint as it expands. “We want to help minimize the environmental impacts of this industry while it develops,” he said.
HARC has a policy playbook designed with what it believes is a roadmap for developers and lawmakers to follow when "managing data center growth."
